sentences.zh: 藝術下

translations.literal: Arts, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Arts and Techniques, Part Two

sentences.zh: 列傳第七十八藝術下

translations.literal: Biographies 78, Arts, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Biography 78: Arts and Techniques, Part Two

sentences.zh: 周澹李修徐謇從孫之才王顯馬嗣明姚僧垣褚該許智藏萬寶常蔣少游何稠

translations.literal: Zhou Dan, Li Xiu, Xu She, Sun Zhicai, Wang Xian, Ma Siming, Yao Sengyuan, Chu Gai, Xu Zhicang, Wan Baochang, Jiang Shaoyou, He Chou
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dan, Li Xiu, Xu She, Sun Zhicai, Wang Xian, Ma Siming, Yao Sengyuan, Chu Gai, Xu Zhicang, Wan Baochang, Jiang Shaoyou, and He Chou

sentences.zh: 周澹，京兆鄠人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Dan was a man of Hu in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dan was a native of Hu County in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 多方術，尤善醫藥，遂為太醫令。

translations.literal: He practiced many arts and was especially good at medicine and drugs, and thus became Grand Physician.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered many arts and was especially skilled in medicine, and in time was appointed Grand Physician.

sentences.zh: 明元嘗苦風頭眩，淡療得愈，由此位特進，賜爵成德侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan once suffered from wind-dizziness in the head; Dan treated him and he recovered. Thereupon his rank was raised to Tejin, and he was granted the title Marquis of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan had once been afflicted with dizzying headaches; Dan cured him, and for this was promoted to Tejin and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 神瑞二年，京師饑，朝議遷都於鄴，淡與博士祭酒崔浩進計，言不可。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenrui the capital suffered famine; the court debated moving the capital to Ye. Dan and the Academician Director Cui Hao submitted a plan saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenrui, famine struck the capital, and the court debated relocating to Ye. Dan and Cui Hao, Director of the Academy, advised against it.

sentences.zh: 明元曰：「唯此二人，與朕意同。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan said: "Only these two men agree with my mind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan said, "Only these two share my view.

sentences.zh: 」詔賜淡、浩妾各一人。

translations.literal: " An edict granted Dan and Hao each one concubine.
translations.idiomatic: " He issued an edict granting Dan and Hao each a concubine.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was given the posthumous name Gong ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 李修，字思祖，本陽平館陶人也。

translations.literal: Li Xiu, style name Sizu, was originally a man of Guantao in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiu, courtesy name Sizu, was originally from Guantao in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 父亮，少學醫術，未能精究。

translations.literal: His father Liang in youth studied medical arts but could not master them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang had studied medicine in his youth but never mastered it fully.

sentences.zh: 太武時奔宋，又就沙門僧坦，略盡其術。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taiwu he fled to Song, and again studied under the monk Sengtan, roughly exhausting his techniques.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Taiwu he fled to the Song court and studied under the monk Sengtan, learning nearly all of his art.

sentences.zh: 針灸授藥，罔不有效。

translations.literal: Whether acupuncture, moxibustion, or administering drugs, none failed to be effective.
translations.idiomatic: Whether by acupuncture, moxibustion, or prescribing medicine, his treatments were invariably effective.

sentences.zh: 徐、兗間，多所救恤。

translations.literal: Between Xu and Yan he saved and relieved many.
translations.idiomatic: Between Xu and Yan provinces he saved and cared for many people.

sentences.zh: 亮大為査事，以舍病人，死者則就而棺殯，親往吊視，其仁厚若此。

translations.literal: Liang greatly undertook charitable works, lodging the sick; when they died he would go and coffin and bury them, personally going to mourn and visit—his benevolence and generosity were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Liang devoted himself to charitable work, taking in the sick; when they died he would personally arrange their coffining and burial and go to mourn them—such was his kindness.

sentences.zh: 累遷府參軍督護。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Military Adjutant and Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Military Adjutant and Supervisor of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本郡士門、宿官，咸相交昵，車馬金帛，酬賚無貲。

translations.literal: The eminent families and veteran officials of his native commandery all associated intimately with him; carriages, horses, gold, and silk—rewards and gifts without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The local gentry and senior officials all sought his company, rewarding him lavishly with carriages, horses, gold, and silk.

sentences.zh: 修兄元孫隨畢眾敬赴平陽，亦遵父業而不及，以功拜奉朝請。

translations.literal: Xiu's elder brother Yuansun followed Bi Zhongjing to Pingyang, also following their father's profession but not reaching his level; for merit he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's elder brother Yuansun followed Bi Zhongjing to Pingyang and likewise practiced their father's craft, though he did not equal Liang; for his service he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 修略與兄同，晚入代京，歷位中散令，以功賜爵下蔡子，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Xiu was roughly the same as his brother; he entered the Dai capital late, served as Palace Attendant, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xia Cai for merit, and was transferred to Attendant Within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was much like his brother; he came to the Northern Wei capital later, served as Palace Attendant, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xia Cai for his merits, and was promoted to Attendant Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 太和中，常在禁內。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was constantly within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he was constantly in attendance within the palace.

sentences.zh: 文明太后時有不豫，修侍針藥多效，賞賜累加，車服第宅，號為鮮麗。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming was unwell, Xiu's attendance with needles and drugs was often effective; rewards piled up, and his carriages, robes, and residence were called splendid.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming fell ill, Xiu's acupuncture and prescriptions proved highly effective; rewards piled up until his carriages, robes, and mansion were renowned for their splendor.

sentences.zh: 集諸學士及工書者百餘人，在東宮撰諸藥方百卷，皆行於世。

translations.literal: He gathered over a hundred scholars and skilled calligraphers and at the Eastern Palace compiled a hundred scrolls of medical formulas, all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled more than a hundred scholars and skilled scribes at the Eastern Palace to compile a hundred-scroll pharmacopoeia, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 先是咸陽公高允雖年且百歲，而氣力尚康，孝文、文明太后時令修診視之。

translations.literal: Earlier, although Duke of Xianyang Gao Yun was nearly a hundred years old, his vital energy and strength were still robust; in the time of Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming they ordered Xiu to examine and treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, although Gao Yun, Duke of Xianyang, was nearly a hundred, he remained vigorous; Emperors Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming had Xiu examine him.

sentences.zh: 一旦，奏言允脈竭氣微，大命無逮，未幾果亡。

translations.literal: One day he memorialized that Yun's pulse was exhausted and his breath faint, and that the great mandate could not be prolonged; before long he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: One day Xiu reported that Yun's pulse was failing and his breath faint—that death was near—and before long Gao Yun did indeed die.

sentences.zh: 後卒于太醫令，贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he died in office as Grand Physician and was posthumously given the title Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Grand Physician and was posthumously appointed Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐謇，字成伯，丹陽人也，家本東莞。

translations.literal: Xu She, style name Chengbo, was a man of Danyang; his family was originally from Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu She, courtesy name Chengbo, was from Danyang, though his family originally came from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 與兄文伯等皆善醫藥。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Wenbo and others were all skilled in medicine and drugs.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Wenbo were all skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 謇因至青州，慕容白曜平東陽，獲之，送京師。

translations.literal: She had gone to Qingzhou; Murong Baiyao pacified Dongyang and captured him, sending him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: She had gone to Qingzhou; when Murong Baiyao conquered Dongyang, he was captured and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 獻文欲驗其能，置病人于幕中，使謇隔而脈之，深得病形，兼知色候，遂被寵遇。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen wished to test his ability; he placed a sick person behind a curtain and had She take the pulse from beyond it. He deeply grasped the form of the illness and also knew color signs, and thus received favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen wished to test his skill: a patient was placed behind a curtain while She took the pulse from outside. He diagnosed the illness precisely and read the patient's complexion as well, and thereafter won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 為中散，稍遷內行長。

translations.literal: He served as Palace Attendant and was gradually promoted to Chief of the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant and was gradually promoted to Chief of the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 文明太后時問經方，而不及李脩之見任用。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming inquired about classical formulas, he did not reach Li Xiu in being employed and used.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming consulted him on medical classics, he was not as favored as Li Xiu.

sentences.zh: 謇合和藥劑攻療之驗，精妙於脩。

translations.literal: She's compounding of drugs and attacking treatment were verified and more refined than Xiu's.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in compounding medicines and administering curative treatments, She proved more skillful than Xiu.

sentences.zh: 而性秘忌。

translations.literal: But his nature was secretive and jealous.
translations.idiomatic: But he was secretive and jealous by nature.

sentences.zh: 承奉不得其意，雖貴為王公，不為措療也。

translations.literal: If service did not accord with his wishes, even if one were ennobled as king or duke, he would not set hand to treatment.
translations.idiomatic: If a patient did not please him, he would refuse treatment even to kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 孝文遷洛，稍加眷待，體小不平，及所寵馮昭儀有病，皆令處療。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, he was somewhat more favored; when the body was slightly unwell, and when his beloved Consort Feng Zhaoyi was ill, all were ordered to have She treat them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, She received greater favor; whenever the emperor felt unwell or his beloved Consort Feng fell ill, She was summoned to treat them.

sentences.zh: 又除中散大夫，轉侍御師。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Palace Attendant Grandee and transferred to Imperial Physician.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Attendant Grandee and then transferred to Imperial Physician.

sentences.zh: 謇欲為孝文合金丹，致延年法，乃入居嵩高，采營其物，曆歲無所成，遂罷。

translations.literal: She wished to compound golden elixir for Emperor Xiaowen to achieve the method of prolonging life; he then entered and dwelt on Songgao, gathering and preparing the materials, but after years achieved nothing and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: She wished to compound an elixir of immortality for Emperor Xiaowen; he retired to Mount Song to gather ingredients, but after years of effort achieved nothing and abandoned the project.

sentences.zh: 二年，上幸縣瓠，有疾大漸，乃馳驛召謇，令水路赴行所，一日一夜行數百里。

translations.literal: In the second year the emperor visited Xianhu and his illness grew grave; he then sent a fast courier to summon She, ordering him to come by water route to the traveling residence, traveling several hundred li in one day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the emperor visited Xianhu and fell gravely ill; a fast courier was sent to summon She, who traveled by water to the imperial camp, covering several hundred li in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 至，診省有大驗。

translations.literal: When he arrived, examination and treatment had great verification.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, his diagnosis and treatment proved highly effective.

sentences.zh: 九月，車駕次於汝濱，乃大為謇設太官珍膳。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the imperial carriage halted at the Ru River bank; a great feast of rare delicacies from the Imperial Kitchen was set for She.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor halted at the Ru River; a grand banquet of imperial delicacies was prepared in She's honor.

sentences.zh: 因集百官，特坐謇于上席，遍陳餚觴於前，命左右宣謇救攝危篤振濟之功，宜加酬齎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered the hundred officials, specially seated She in the upper place, spread dishes and cups before all, and ordered attendants to proclaim She's merit in rescuing the gravely ill and reviving the dying, saying rewards should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then assembled the officials, seated She in the place of honor, and had attendants proclaim his merit in saving the emperor from mortal illness—merit deserving generous reward.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔褒美，以謇為大鴻臚卿、金卿縣伯，又賜錢絹、雜物、奴婢、牛馬，事出豐厚，皆經內呈。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict praising him, appointing She as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Baron of Jinxiang County, and also bestowing money, silk, miscellaneous goods, male and female servants, cattle and horses—the gifts were lavish, all presented through the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of praise followed: She was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Baron of Jinxiang, with lavish gifts of money, silk, goods, servants, cattle, and horses—all presented through the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 諸親王咸陽王禧等各有別齎，並至千匹。

translations.literal: The various imperial princes including Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi each had separate gifts, all reaching a thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial princes, including Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi, each sent separate gifts amounting to a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 從行至鄴，上猶自發動，謇日夕左右。

translations.literal: Accompanying the journey to Ye, the emperor still had relapses; She attended day and night at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the emperor to Ye, She attended him day and night as relapses continued.

sentences.zh: 明年，從詣馬圈，上疾勢遂甚，蹙蹙不怡，每加切誚，又欲加之鞭捶，幸而獲免。

translations.literal: The next year, following to the horse park, the emperor's illness grew severe; he was fretful and displeased, constantly adding sharp rebukes, and again wished to add whipping—fortunately She escaped it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, at the horse park, the emperor's condition worsened; fretful and irritable, he rebuked She harshly and even threatened to whip him—though She narrowly escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝崩後，謇隨梓宮還洛。

translations.literal: After the emperor's death, She followed the coffin back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death, She accompanied the coffin back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 文伯仕南齊，位東莞、太山、蘭陵三郡太守。

translations.literal: Wenbo served the Southern Qi, holding the posts of Administrator of the three commanderies Dongguan, Taishan, and Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo served the Southern Qi as Administrator of Dongguan, Taishan, and Lanling in succession.

sentences.zh: 子雄，員外散騎侍郎，醫術為江左所稱，事並見《南史》。

translations.literal: His son Xiong, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier, had medical arts praised in the Jiangzuo region; the affairs are all seen in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier, was renowned in the south for his medical skill; his story is recorded in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 雄子之才，幼而俊發，五歲誦《孝經》，八歲略通義旨。

translations.literal: Xiong's son Zhicai in youth was brilliant and quick; at five he recited the Classic of Filial Piety, and at eight he roughly understood its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's son Zhicai was precocious: at five he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, and at eight he grasped its meaning.

sentences.zh: 曾與從兄康造梁太子詹事汝南周舍宅，聽《老子》。

translations.literal: He once with his cousin Kang visited the residence of Zhou She of Runan, Tutor to the Heir Apparent of Liang, to hear the Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Once, with his cousin Kang, he visited the home of Zhou She of Runan, Tutor to the Liang heir apparent, to hear a lecture on the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 舍為設食，乃戲之曰：「徐郎不用心思義，而但事食乎？

translations.literal: Zhou set out food and then jested with him, saying: "Young Xu, you do not use your mind on righteousness but only attend to eating?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou provided a meal and teased him: "Young Xu, are you thinking about the Way, or only about your meal?

sentences.zh: 」之才答曰：「蓋聞聖人虛其心而實其腹。

translations.literal: " Zhicai replied: "I have heard that the sage empties his mind but fills his belly.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhicai replied, "I have heard that the sage empties his mind but fills his belly.

sentences.zh: 」舍嗟賞之。

translations.literal: " Zhou sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 年十三，召為太學生，粗通《禮》、《易》。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he was summoned as an Imperial University student and roughly mastered the Rites and the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he entered the Imperial University and gained a working knowledge of the Rites and the Changes.

sentences.zh: 彭城劉孝綽、河東裴子野、吳郡張嵊等每共論《周易》及《喪服》儀，酬應如響。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaochuo of Pengcheng, Pei Ziye of Hedong, Zhang Sheng of Wu commandery and others whenever together discussed the Zhouyi and mourning-garment rites; his responses were like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xiaochuo, Pei Ziye, Zhang Sheng, and others debated the Book of Changes and mourning rites, Zhicai's replies came as swiftly as echoes.

sentences.zh: 咸共歎曰：「此神童也。

translations.literal: They all together sighed and said: "This is a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: They all exclaimed, "This is a prodigy!

sentences.zh: 」孝綽又云：「徐郎燕頷，有班定遠之相。

translations.literal: " Xiaochuo also said: "Young Xu's swallow jaw has the appearance of Ban Chao.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaochuo added, "Young Xu has the jaw of a swallow—he has the bearing of Ban Chao the Far-Reaching.

sentences.zh: 」陳郡袁昂丹陽尹，辟為主簿，人務事宜，皆被顧訪。

translations.literal: " Yuan Ang of Chen commandery, Administrator of Danyang, recruited him as Chief Clerk; whenever people had official business, all were attended and consulted.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Ang of Chen commandery, Administrator of Danyang, appointed him Chief Clerk; on all matters of administration he was consulted.

sentences.zh: 郡廨遭火，之才起望，夜中不著衣，披紅眠帕出房，映光為昂所見。

translations.literal: The prefectural offices caught fire; Zhicai rose to look out, and in the middle of the night without putting on clothes, draped in a red sleeping kerchief he came out of the room—the light reflected and Yuan Ang saw him.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectural offices caught fire, Zhicai rushed out at night without dressing, wrapped only in a red sleeping scarf—and Yuan Ang saw him in the firelight.

sentences.zh: 功曹白請免職，昂重其才術，仍特原之。

translations.literal: The Merit Officer reported requesting dismissal from office; Ang valued his talent and skill and still specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Merit Officer recommended his dismissal, but Yuan Ang, valuing his talent, specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 豫章王綜出鎮江都，復除豫章王國左常侍，又轉綜鎮北主簿。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Zong went out to garrison Jiangdu; Zhicai was again appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Yuzhang princedom, then transferred to Chief Clerk of Zong's Northern Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yuzhang Zong was posted to Jiangdu, Zhicai was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the princedom and then Chief Clerk of the Northern Garrison staff.

sentences.zh: 及綜入魏，三軍散走，之才退至呂梁，橋斷路絕，遂為魏統軍石茂孫所止。

translations.literal: When Zong entered Wei, the three armies scattered and fled; Zhicai retreated to Liang and was stopped when the bridge was broken and the road cut off, and was detained by the Wei commander Shi Maosun.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong defected to Wei and the army scattered, Zhicai retreated to Liang, but with bridges destroyed and roads cut off he was detained by the Wei commander Shi Maosun.

sentences.zh: 綜入魏旬月，位至司空。

translations.literal: Within a month of Zong's entering Wei, his rank reached Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of Zong's arrival in Wei, he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏聽綜收斂僚屬，乃訪知之才在彭泗。

translations.literal: Wei permitted Zong to gather his staff; he then inquired and learned Zhicai was at Peng and Si.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court allowed Zong to gather his staff; he learned that Zhicai was in the Peng-Si region.

sentences.zh: 啟魏帝，雲之才大善醫術，兼有機辯。

translations.literal: He reported to the Wei emperor, saying Zhicai was greatly skilled in medical arts and also had quick wit in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the Wei emperor that Zhicai was highly skilled in medicine and quick-witted besides.

sentences.zh: 詔征之才。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Zhicai.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued summoning Zhicai.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，至洛，敕居南館，禮遇甚優。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang he arrived at Luoyang; he was ordered to reside in the Southern Lodge and received very generous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang he arrived in Luoyang and was lodged in the Southern Residence with generous treatment.

sentences.zh: 謇子踐啟求之才還宅。

translations.literal: She's son Jian submitted a memorial requesting Zhicai be allowed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: She's son Jian petitioned for Zhicai to be allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 之才藥石多效，又窺涉經史，發言辨捷，朝賢競相耍引，為之延譽。

translations.literal: Zhicai's drugs and stones were often effective; he also glanced into the classics and histories, and when he spoke was quick in debate; court worthies competed to draw him in and spread his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai's prescriptions were highly effective; versed in the classics and histories, he spoke with quick wit, and court officials competed to befriend him and spread his fame.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，封昌安縣侯。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 天平中，齊神武征赴晉陽，常在內館，禮遇稍厚。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, when Qi Shenwu summoned him to Jinyang, he was constantly in the inner lodge and received somewhat thicker treatment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era, when Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang, he resided in the inner quarters and received still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 武定四年，自散騎常侍轉秘書監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wuding he was transferred from Attendant Cavalier to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wuding he was transferred from Attendant Cavalier to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文宣作相，普加黜陟，楊愔以其南士，不堪典掌功程，且多陪從，全廢曹務，轉授金紫光祿大夫，以魏收代。

translations.literal: When Wensuan became Chancellor, there was a general round of dismissals and promotions; Yang Yin, because he was a southern gentleman, was unfit to manage and oversee construction projects, and moreover often accompanied and attended, completely neglecting bureau duties—he was transferred and given the post of Grand Master of the Golden Gate and Purple Enclosure, with Wei Shou replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan became Chancellor, Yang Yin judged that Zhicai, as a southerner, was unfit to oversee construction projects and spent too much time in attendance, neglecting his duties; he was transferred to Grand Master of the Golden Gate and Purple Enclosure, with Wei Shou replacing him.

sentences.zh: 之才甚怏怏不平。

translations.literal: Zhicai was very displeased and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 之才少解天文，兼圖讖之學，共館客宋景業參校吉凶，知午年必有革易。

translations.literal: Zhicai in youth understood astronomy and also the learning of charts and prophecies; with lodge guest Song Jingye he examined good and ill fortune and knew that in a wu year there would certainly be revolution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai had studied astronomy and prophecy; with his colleague Song Jingye he divined that a wu year would bring revolution.

sentences.zh: 因高德正啟之，文宣聞而大悅。

translations.literal: Through Gao Dezheng he reported this; Wensuan heard and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this through Gao Dezheng; Wenxuan was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 時自婁太后及勳貴臣咸云：「關西既是勍敵，恐其有挾天子令諸侯之辭，不可先行禪代事。

translations.literal: At the time from Empress Dowager Lou and the meritorious nobles all said: "The Guanxi region is already a formidable enemy; we fear they have the argument of holding the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords—it is not permissible to first carry out the abdication and succession.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Empress Dowager Lou and the meritorious nobles all argued: "The west is a formidable enemy; they may use the emperor as a hostage to command the lords—we must not rush the abdication.

sentences.zh: 」之才獨云：「千人逐兔，一人得之，諸人咸息。

translations.literal: " Zhicai alone said: "A thousand men chase a rabbit; when one man obtains it, all the others cease.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhicai alone argued: "When a thousand men chase a rabbit, once one catches it the rest stop.

sentences.zh: 須定大業，何容翻欲學人？

translations.literal: The great enterprise must be settled—how can one turn around and wish to imitate others?
translations.idiomatic: The great enterprise must be settled—why hesitate to imitate others?

sentences.zh: 」又援引證據，備有條目，帝從之。

translations.literal: " He again cited evidence, fully furnished with entries; the emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He cited further evidence in detail, and the emperor followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 登阼後，彌見親密。

translations.literal: After ascending the throne, he was increasingly seen as intimate.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenxuan took the throne, Zhicai grew still closer to him.

sentences.zh: 之才非惟醫術自進，亦為首唱禪代，又戲謔滑稽，言無不至，於是大被狎昵。

translations.literal: Zhicai not only advanced through medical arts but also was the first to advocate the abdication and succession; moreover he jested and was comical, speaking without limit—thus he was greatly treated with familiar intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai had advanced not only through medicine but as the foremost advocate of the dynastic transition; witty and irreverent, he spoke without restraint and was treated with great familiarity.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，封池陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant Within and enfeoffed as Baron of Chiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Attendant Within and enfeoffed as Baron of Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 見文宣政令轉嚴，求出，除趙州刺史。

translations.literal: Seeing Wensuan's government orders growing strict, he sought to leave and was appointed Governor of Zhao province.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wenxuan's rule grow harsh, he sought a post outside the capital and was appointed Governor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 竟不獲述職，猶為弄臣。

translations.literal: In the end he did not obtain to assume his duties and remained a court jester.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up the post and remained a court entertainer.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年，除西兗州刺史，未之官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangjian he was appointed Governor of Western Yan province but did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he was appointed Governor of Western Yan but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 武明皇太后不豫，之才療之，應手便愈，孝昭賜彩帛千段、錦四百匹。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wuming was unwell, Zhicai treated her and she recovered at once; Emperor Xiaozhao bestowed a thousand lengths of colored silk and four hundred bolts of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wuming fell ill, Zhicai cured her instantly; Emperor Xiaozhao rewarded him with a thousand lengths of silk and four hundred bolts of brocade.

sentences.zh: 之才既善醫術，雖有外授，頃即征還。

translations.literal: Since Zhicai was skilled in medical arts, although he had an outside appointment, shortly he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his medical skill, though appointed to provincial posts he was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 既博識多聞，由是于方術尤妙。

translations.literal: Since he was broadly learned and heard much, thereby in arts and techniques he was especially marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned, he became especially skilled in divination and the occult arts.

sentences.zh: 大寧二年春，武明太后又病，之才弟之范為尚藥典禦，敕令診候。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Daning, Empress Dowager Wuming was ill again; Zhicai's younger brother Zhifan was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy and was ordered to examine and attend.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Daning, Empress Dowager Wuming fell ill again; Zhicai's brother Zhifan, Director of the Imperial Pharmacy, was ordered to examine her.

sentences.zh: 內史皆令呼太后為石婆，蓋有欲忌，故改名以厭制之。

translations.literal: The inner secretaries all ordered that the Empress Dowager be called Stone Granny, probably because of taboo avoidance, so they changed the name to suppress and control it.
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretaries had everyone call the empress dowager "Old Stone Woman," changing her title to ward off ill omens through taboo avoidance.

sentences.zh: 之範出告之才曰：「童謠云：'周裏跂求伽，豹祠嫁石婆，斬塚作媒人，唯得一量紫綖靴。

translations.literal: Zhifan went out and told Zhicai: "A children's song says: 'Within Zhou, Qi begged for Jia; at the Leopard Shrine they marry Stone Granny; the beheaded mound serves as matchmaker—only obtaining one measure of purple silk boots.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhifan told Zhicai, "A children's rhyme runs: 'Within Zhou, Qi begged for Jia; at the Leopard Shrine they marry Old Stone Woman; the beheaded mound is the matchmaker—only a measure of purple silk boots is gained.'

sentences.zh: '今太后忽改名，私所致怪。

translations.literal: ' Now the Empress Dowager has suddenly had her name changed—this privately causes strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: ' Now they have suddenly renamed the empress dowager—this privately alarms me.

sentences.zh: 」之才曰：「跂求伽，胡言去已，豹祠嫁石婆，豈有好事？

translations.literal: " Zhicai said: "'Qi begged for Jia'—barbarian speech meaning 'gone already'; 'Leopard Shrine marries Stone Granny'—how could there be a good outcome?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhicai said, "'Qi begged for Jia' is barbarian speech for 'already gone'; 'Leopard Shrine marries Old Stone Woman'—can that portend anything good?

sentences.zh: 斬塚作媒人，但令合葬，自斬塚。

translations.literal: 'The beheaded mound as matchmaker'—only means joint burial; one buries oneself at the beheaded mound.
translations.idiomatic: 'The beheaded mound as matchmaker' means only joint burial—she will be buried at the beheaded mound.

sentences.zh: 唯得紫綖靴者，得至四月。

translations.literal: 'Only obtaining purple silk boots'—she will reach the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: 'Only a measure of purple silk boots' means she will live until the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 紫之為字，此下系，綖者熟，當在四月之中。

translations.literal: The character for purple—below this is 'silk thread'; 'xian' means ripe—this should be in the middle of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the character zi (purple), below is si (silk); xian means 'ripe'—she will die in mid-April.

sentences.zh: 」之范問靴是何義。

translations.literal: " Zhifan asked what the meaning of 'boots' was.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhifan asked what 'boots' signified.

sentences.zh: 之才曰：「靴者革旁化，寧是久物？

translations.literal: Zhicai said: "'Boots'—beside 'leather' is 'transform'; surely this is not a lasting thing?
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "'Boots'—with 'leather' beside it becomes 'transform'; surely this cannot mean long life?

sentences.zh: 」至四月一日，後果崩。

translations.literal: " On the first day of the fourth month, the Empress Dowager indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month, she died as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 有人患腳跟腫痛，諸醫莫能識。

translations.literal: Someone suffered swollen painful heels; none of the physicians could identify it.
translations.idiomatic: A patient suffered swollen, painful heels that no physician could diagnose.

sentences.zh: 之才曰：「蛤精疾也，由乘船入海，垂腳水中。

translations.literal: Zhicai said: "This is clam-spirit illness, caused by taking a boat onto the sea and dangling one's feet in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "This is clam-spirit sickness—from sailing on the sea with one's feet hanging in the water.

sentences.zh: 」疾者曰：「實曾如此。

translations.literal: " The sick man said: "I indeed did so.
translations.idiomatic: The patient said, "That is exactly what happened.

sentences.zh: 」之才為剖，得蛤子二，大如榆莢。

translations.literal: " Zhicai cut it open and obtained two clam seeds, as large as elm pods.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai lanced the swelling and removed two clam larvae the size of elm pods.

sentences.zh: 又有以骨為刀子把者，五色斑斕。

translations.literal: There was also someone who used bone for a knife handle, five-colored and mottled.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had made a knife handle from bone, mottled in five colors.

sentences.zh: 之才曰：「此人瘤也。

translations.literal: Zhicai said: "This person has a tumor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "This man has a tumor.

sentences.zh: 」問得處，云：「于古塚見髑髏，額骨長數寸，試削視，有文理，故用之。

translations.literal: " Asked where he obtained it, he said: "In an ancient tomb I saw a skull; the forehead bone was several inches long. I tried shaving it to look and found grain patterns, so I used it.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where he got it, the man said he had found a skull in an ancient tomb; the forehead bone was several inches long, and when he shaved it he found grain patterns, so he used it.

sentences.zh: 」其明悟多通如此。

translations.literal: " His clear insight and broad understanding were like this.
translations.idiomatic: His keen insight was often demonstrated in such ways.

sentences.zh: 天統四年，累遷尚書左僕射，俄除兗州刺史，特給鐃吹一部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiantong he was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and soon appointed Governor of Yan province, specially granted a set of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiantong he rose to Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, then was appointed Governor of Yan with a special grant of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 之才醫術最高，偏被命召。

translations.literal: Zhicai's medical art was supreme and he was especially summoned by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: His medical skill was supreme, and he was frequently summoned by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 武成酒色過度，怳忽不恆。

translations.literal: Wucheng exceeded in wine and women and was unsettled and unsteady.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng indulged excessively in wine and women and was often unsettled.

sentences.zh: 曾病發，自雲，初見空中有五色物，稍近，變成一美婦人，去地數丈，亭亭而立。

translations.literal: Once when his illness broke out, he himself said that at first he saw a five-colored object in the air; as it drew nearer it turned into a beautiful woman, several zhang from the ground, standing erect.
translations.idiomatic: During one attack he said he first saw a five-colored object in the air that, as it drew near, became a beautiful woman standing several zhang above the ground.

sentences.zh: 食頃，變為觀世音。

translations.literal: After the time it takes to eat, it turned into Guanyin.
translations.idiomatic: After the time of a meal it transformed into Guanyin.

sentences.zh: 之才云：「此色欲多，大虛所致。

translations.literal: Zhicai said: "This comes from excessive lust and great depletion of vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "This comes from excessive lust and great depletion of vital energy.

sentences.zh: 」即處湯方，服一劑，便覺稍遠；

translations.literal: " He then prescribed a decoction; after one dose he felt it recede somewhat;
translations.idiomatic: He prescribed a decoction; after one dose the vision receded somewhat;

sentences.zh: 又服，還變成五色物；

translations.literal: after another dose it turned back into a five-colored object;
translations.idiomatic: after another dose it turned back into a five-colored object;

sentences.zh: 數劑湯，疾竟愈。

translations.literal: after several doses of decoction the illness was completely cured.
translations.idiomatic: after several more doses the illness was completely cured.

sentences.zh: 帝每發動，暫遣騎追之，針藥所加，應時必效，故頻有端執之舉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor had a relapse, he would temporarily send a fast rider to pursue him; needles and drugs applied were effective at once, and thus there were frequent instances of holding him in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor relapsed, a fast rider was sent to fetch him; his treatments took effect immediately, and he was often kept in attendance.

sentences.zh: 入秋，武成小定，更不發動。

translations.literal: Entering autumn, Wucheng was somewhat settled and no longer had relapses.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Wucheng stabilized and had no further relapses.

sentences.zh: 和士開欲依次轉進，以之才附籍兗州，即是本屬，遂奏附除刺史，以胡長仁為左僕射，士開為右僕射。

translations.literal: He Shikai wished to advance in turn according to rank; because Zhicai was registered in Yan province, which was his native jurisdiction, he memorialized that Zhicai be additionally appointed Governor, with Hu Changren as Left Vice Minister and He Shikai as Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai wished to advance by seniority; because Zhicai was registered in Yan, his home province, he had Zhicai appointed governor, with Hu Changren as Left Vice Minister and himself as Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 及十月，帝又病動，語士開云：「浪用之才外任，使我辛苦。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the emperor's illness relapsed again; he told He Shikai: "You wastefully placed Zhicai in an outside post, making me suffer.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor relapsed and told He Shikai, "You wastefully sent Zhicai away, making me suffer.

sentences.zh: 」其月八日，敕驛追之才。

translations.literal: " On the eighth of that month an edict sent a fast courier to summon Zhicai.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth of that month an edict sent a fast courier to summon Zhicai.

sentences.zh: 帝以十日崩，之才十一日方到。

translations.literal: The emperor died on the tenth; Zhicai arrived only on the eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died on the tenth; Zhicai arrived on the eleventh.

sentences.zh: 既無所及，復還赴州。

translations.literal: Since there was nothing more to be done, he returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: There was nothing he could do, and he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 在職無所侵暴，但不甚閑法理，頗亦疏慢，用舍自由。

translations.literal: In office he committed no oppression or violence, but he was not very versed in legal principles and was rather negligent and lax, acting as he pleased in appointments and dismissals.
translations.idiomatic: In office he did not oppress the people, but he was not well versed in law and was rather negligent, appointing and dismissing at will.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，後主征之才。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year the Later Lord summoned Zhicai.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year the Later Lord summoned Zhicai.

sentences.zh: 尋左僕射闕，之才曰：「自可復禹之績。

translations.literal: Soon the Left Vice Minister post was vacant; Zhicai said: "I can myself resume Yu's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Left Vice Minister post fell vacant, Zhicai said, "I can resume Yu the Great's work.

sentences.zh: 」武平元年，重除尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Wuping he was again appointed Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was again appointed Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 之才於和士開、陸令萱母子曲盡卑狎，二家若疾，救護百端。

translations.literal: Zhicai toward He Shikai and Lu Lingxuan mother and son bent to the utmost in servility and intimacy; when either household was ill, he attended with a hundred remedies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai fawned on He Shikai and Lu Lingxuan and their son, attending them with every remedy when they fell ill.

sentences.zh: 由是遷尚書令，封西陽郡王。

translations.literal: Thereby he was promoted to Minister of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to Minister of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖珽執政，除之才侍中、太子太師。

translations.literal: When Zu Ting took power, Zhicai was appointed Attendant Within and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ting took power, Zhicai was appointed Attendant Within and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 之才恨曰：「子野沙汰我。

translations.literal: Zhicai resentfully said: "Ziye has sifted me out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said resentfully, "Ziye has sifted me out.

sentences.zh: 」珽目疾，故以師曠比之。

translations.literal: " Ting had eye disease, so he compared him to Music Master Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting was blind, so Zhicai compared him to the blind music master Kuang.

sentences.zh: 之才聰辯強識，有兼人之敏。

translations.literal: Zhicai was clever in debate and strong in memory, with the quickness of one who excels others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai was clever in debate and possessed a prodigious memory.

sentences.zh: 尤好劇談體語，公私言聚，多相嘲戲。

translations.literal: He especially loved witty talk and colloquial speech; whenever people gathered in public or private, they often mocked one another.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved witty repartee; at gatherings public and private, banter and mockery flowed freely.

sentences.zh: 鄭道育常戲之才為師公，之才曰：「既為汝師，又為汝公，在三之義，頓居其兩。

translations.literal: Zheng Daoyu often jested with Zhicai as 'Teacher Duke'; Zhicai said: "Since I am your teacher, I am also your duke—in the three relationships I suddenly occupy two.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Daoyu nicknamed him 'Teacher Duke'; Zhicai replied, "I am both your teacher and your duke—in the three bonds of relationship I hold two at once.

sentences.zh: 」又嘲王昕姓云：「有言則訁王，近犬便狂，加頸足而為馬，施角尾而成羊。

translations.literal: " He also mocked Wang Xin's surname, saying: "With speech it is Wang 'argue'; near a dog it becomes 'mad'; add neck and legs and it becomes a horse; add horns and tail and it becomes a sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked Wang Xin's surname: "Add speech and it is 'argue'; near a dog it is 'mad'; add neck and legs for 'horse'; add horns and tail for 'sheep.

sentences.zh: 」盧元明因戲之才云：「卿姓是未入人，名是子之誤，之當為之也。

translations.literal: " Lu Yuanming therefore jested with Zhicai: "Your surname is 'not yet entered person'; your given name is the error of 'son'—it should be 'this'.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanming jested, "Your surname means 'not yet a person'; your given name is a mistake for 'son'—it should be 'this.

sentences.zh: 」即答云：「卿姓，在上為虐，在丘為虛，生男則為虜，配馬則為驢。

translations.literal: " He immediately replied: "Your surname—above is 'tyrant,' on a mound is 'empty'; born a male you are a 'captive,' matched with a horse you are an 'ass.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your surname—above is 'tyrant,' on a hill is 'empty'; a male child is a 'captive,' paired with a horse an 'ass.

sentences.zh: 」又常與朝士出遊，遙望群犬競走，諸人試令目之。

translations.literal: " He also often went out with court gentlemen; from afar they saw a pack of dogs running; the others tried to have him identify them.
translations.idiomatic: Once on an outing with court gentlemen they saw dogs running; the others asked him to identify them.

sentences.zh: 之才即應聲云：「為是宋鵲？

translations.literal: Zhicai immediately responded: "Is it Song Que?
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai instantly replied, "Is it Song Que?

sentences.zh: 為是韓盧？

translations.literal: Is it Han Lu?
translations.idiomatic: Is it Han Lu?

sentences.zh: 為逐李斯東走？

translations.literal: Is it chasing Li Si eastward?
translations.idiomatic: Is it chasing Li Si eastward?

sentences.zh: 為負帝女南徂？

translations.literal: Is it carrying the Emperor's daughter southward?
translations.idiomatic: Is it carrying the Emperor's daughter southward?

sentences.zh: 」李諧於廣坐因稱其父名曰：「卿嗜熊白生不？

translations.literal: " Li He in a great assembly therefore spoke his father's name, saying: "Do you relish raw bear paw?
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Li He deliberately spoke his father's name: "Do you relish raw bear paw?

sentences.zh: 」之才曰：「平平耳。

translations.literal: " Zhicai said: "So-so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "So-so.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「卿此言于理平不？

translations.literal: " He also said: "Does your statement accord with reason or not?
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Is that statement reasonable or not?

sentences.zh: 」諧遽出避之，道逢其甥高德正。

translations.literal: " He hastily went out to avoid him and on the road met his nephew Gao Dezheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li He fled and met his nephew Gao Dezheng on the way.

sentences.zh: 德正曰：「舅顏色何不悅？

translations.literal: Dezheng said: "Uncle, why is your expression not pleased?
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng asked, "Uncle, why do you look displeased?

sentences.zh: 」諧告之故。

translations.literal: " He told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Li He told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 德正徑造坐席，連索熊白。

translations.literal: Dezheng went straight to the seat and repeatedly demanded bear paw.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng went straight to the table and loudly demanded bear paw.

sentences.zh: 之才謂坐者曰：「個人諱底？

translations.literal: Zhicai said to those seated: "Whose taboo is this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai asked the company, "Whose taboo is this?

sentences.zh: 」眾莫之應。

translations.literal: " None responded.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 之才曰：「生不為人所知，死不為人所諱，此何足問。

translations.literal: Zhicai said: "Alive he was unknown to others; dead he is not tabooed by others—what is there to ask?
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai said, "Alive he was unknown; dead he needs no taboo—what is there to ask?

sentences.zh: 」唐邕、白建方貴，時人言云：「并州赫赫唐與白。

translations.literal: " Tang Yong and Bai Jian were then in high favor; people said: "In Bingzhou, Tang and Bai blaze.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong and Bai Jian were then powerful; people said, "In Bingzhou, Tang and Bai blaze.

sentences.zh: 」之才茂之。

translations.literal: " Zhicai envied them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai envied them.

sentences.zh: 元日，對邕為諸令史祝曰：「卿等位當作唐、白。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, facing Yong he offered a toast to the clerks: "You gentlemen's posts ought to become Tang and Bai.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day he toasted the clerks before Tang Yong: "Your posts should become Tang and Bai.

sentences.zh: 」又以小史好嚼筆，故常執管就元文遙口曰：「借君齒。

translations.literal: " He also because a junior clerk loved to chew brush tips would often hold the brush tube to Yuan Wen's mouth from afar and say: "Lend me your teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Because a junior clerk chewed brush tips, he would hold a brush to Yuan Wen's mouth and say, "Lend me your teeth.

sentences.zh: 」其不遜如此。

translations.literal: " His insolence was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his insolence.

sentences.zh: 曆事諸帝，以戲狎得寵。

translations.literal: Serving successive emperors, he won favor through jesting intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He served successive emperors and won favor through jesting intimacy.

sentences.zh: 武成生齻牙，問諸醫，尚藥典禦鄧宣文以實對，武成怒而撻之。

translations.literal: Wucheng was born with projecting teeth; he asked the physicians, and the Director of the Imperial Pharmacy Deng Xuanwen answered truthfully; Wucheng in anger flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng was born with projecting teeth; when the Director of the Imperial Pharmacy Deng Xuanwen told the truth, Wucheng had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 後以問之才，拜賀曰：「此是智牙，生智牙者，聰明長壽。

translations.literal: Later when he asked Zhicai, Zhicai bowed in congratulation and said: "These are wisdom teeth; one who bears wisdom teeth is intelligent and long-lived.
translations.idiomatic: When he asked Zhicai, Zhicai bowed and said, "These are wisdom teeth; those who have them are intelligent and long-lived.

sentences.zh: 」武成悅而賞之。

translations.literal: " Wucheng was pleased and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng was pleased and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 為僕射時，語人曰：「我在江東，見徐勉作僕射，朝士莫不佞之。

translations.literal: When he was Vice Minister he said to people: "In the Jiangdong I saw Xu Mian as Vice Minister—all court gentlemen fawned on him.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Minister he said, "In the south I saw Xu Mian as Vice Minister—every courtier fawned on him.

sentences.zh: 今我亦是徐僕射，無一人佞我，何由可活！

translations.literal: Now I too am Vice Minister Xu—yet not one person fawns on me; how can I survive!
translations.idiomatic: Now I too am Vice Minister Xu—yet no one fawns on me; how can I survive!

sentences.zh: 」之才妻，魏廣陽王妹，之才從文襄求得為妻。

translations.literal: " Zhicai's wife was the sister of the Prince of Guangyang of Wei; Zhicai obtained her as wife through Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai's wife was a sister of the Prince of Guangyang; he obtained her through Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 和士開知之，乃淫其妻。

translations.literal: He Shikai learned of this and then violated his wife.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai learned of this and seduced his wife.

sentences.zh: 之才遇見而避之，退曰：「妨少年戲笑。

translations.literal: Zhicai encountered them and avoided them, withdrawing and saying: "I disturb the young people's sport.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai came upon them and withdrew, saying, "I disturb the young people's sport.

sentences.zh: 」其縱之如此。

translations.literal: " His indulgence was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his indulgence.

sentences.zh: 年八十，卒，贈司徒公、錄尚書事，諡曰文明。

translations.literal: At age eighty he died and was posthumously given the titles Duke of the Secretariat and Recorder of the Affairs of the Master of Writing, with posthumous name Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously appointed Duke of the Secretariat and Recorder of the Affairs of the Master of Writing, with the posthumous name Wenming.

sentences.zh: 長子林，字少卿，太尉司馬。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lin, style name Shaoqing, was Marshal of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lin, courtesy name Shaoqing, was Marshal of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 次子同卿，太子庶子。

translations.literal: His second son Tongqing was Aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Tongqing was Aide to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 之才以其無學術，每歎曰：「終恐同《廣陵散》矣。」

translations.literal: Zhicai, because they had no learning, often sighed: "In the end I fear it will be like the 'Guangling San.'"
translations.idiomatic: Because they lacked learning, Zhicai often sighed, "In the end I fear it will be like the Guangling San."

sentences.zh: 弟之范亦醫術見知，位太常卿，特聽襲之才爵西陽王。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhifan was also renowned for medical arts, holding the post of Minister of Ceremonies, and was specially permitted to inherit Zhicai's title as Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhifan was also renowned in medicine, served as Minister of Ceremonies, and was permitted to inherit the title Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 入周，授儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Entering Zhou, he was appointed General with the prestige of Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou conquest he was appointed General of Yitong.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 王顯，字世榮，陽平樂平人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xian, style name Shirong, was a man of Yueping in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian, courtesy name Shirong, was from Yueping in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 自言本東海郯人，王朗之後也。

translations.literal: He himself said his family was originally from Tan in Donghai, a descendant of Wang Lang.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Wang Lang of Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 父安上，少與李亮同師，俱受醫藥，而不及亮。

translations.literal: His father Anshang in youth studied with Li Liang as fellow students, both receiving medical arts, but did not reach Liang's level.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anshang studied medicine with Li Liang but did not equal him.

sentences.zh: 顯少曆本州從事，雖以醫術自通，而明敏有決斷才用。

translations.literal: Xian in youth served as an aide in his native province; although he made his way through medical arts, he was bright and keen with decisive talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xian served as a provincial aide in his youth; though he practiced medicine, he was bright and decisive.

sentences.zh: 初文昭太后之懷宣武，夢為日所逐，化而為龍而繞後，後寤而驚悸，遂成心疾。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenzhao was pregnant with Emperor Xuanwu, she dreamed she was pursued by the sun, which transformed into a dragon that coiled behind her; when she awoke she was startled and fearful, and thus developed heart illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenzhao was pregnant with Emperor Xuanwu, she dreamed the sun pursued her and became a dragon coiling behind her; she awoke terrified and developed heart illness.

sentences.zh: 文明太后敕徐謇及顯等為後診脈，謇雲是微風入藏，宜進湯加針。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered Xu She and Xian and others to examine her pulse; She said it was a slight wind entering the viscera and that soup and needles should be administered.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had Xu She and Xian examine her; She said a slight wind had entered the viscera and prescribed decoction and acupuncture.

sentences.zh: 顯言案三部脈，非有心疾，將是懷孕生男之象。

translations.literal: Xian said that examining the three pulse positions, it was not heart illness but rather the sign of pregnancy bearing a male.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said that examining the three pulse positions showed not heart illness but pregnancy with a male child.

sentences.zh: 果如顯言。

translations.literal: It turned out as Xian had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved Xian correct.

sentences.zh: 久之，補待禦師。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Imperial Physician.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was appointed Imperial Physician.

sentences.zh: 宣武自幼有微疾，顯攝療有效，因稍蒙眄識。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu from childhood had a slight illness; Xian treated him with effect and thus gradually received notice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu had a minor ailment from childhood; Xian treated him effectively and gradually won notice.

sentences.zh: 又罷六輔之初，顯為領軍於烈間通規策，頗有密功。

translations.literal: Also at the beginning of the dismissal of the Six Regents, Xian between Yu Lie of the General-in-Chief communicated secret stratagems and had considerable hidden merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the dismissal of the Six Regents, Xian conveyed secret plans to Yu Lie, the General-in-Chief, and rendered considerable hidden service.

sentences.zh: 累遷廷尉卿，仍在侍御，營進禦藥，出入禁內。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Justice and still attended the emperor, managing and advancing imperial drugs, entering and leaving the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Justice while still attending the emperor, preparing imperial medicines within the palace.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 顯前後居職，所在著稱。

translations.literal: Wherever Xian held office before and after, he was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held, Xian won renown.

sentences.zh: 糾折庶獄，究其奸回，出內惜慎，憂國如家。

translations.literal: He investigated and corrected ordinary cases, pursued the crafty and rebellious, and in going out and coming in was cautious and careful, grieving for the state as for his own family.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated cases, pursued wrongdoing, and was cautious in conduct, grieving for the state as for his own household.

sentences.zh: 及領憲台，多所彈劾，百僚肅然。

translations.literal: When he headed the Censorate he impeached many; the hundred officials were awed.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Censorate he impeached many, and officials stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 又以中尉屬官不悉稱職，諷求改革。

translations.literal: Also because the subordinate officials of the Censor-in-Chief were not all competent, he subtly sought reform.
translations.idiomatic: Finding subordinates of the Censorate incompetent, he sought reform.

sentences.zh: 詔委改選，務盡才能。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted the reselection, striving to employ men of full ability.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered reselection of personnel with full regard to ability.

sentences.zh: 而顯所舉，或有請屬，未皆得人，於是眾議喧嘩，聲望致損。

translations.literal: But those Xian recommended sometimes had patronage requests and were not all the right men; thereupon public discussion was noisy and his reputation was damaged.
translations.idiomatic: But some of his appointees owed their posts to patronage, and public criticism damaged his reputation.

sentences.zh: 後宣武詔顯撰藥方三十五卷，班布天下，以療諸疾。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xuanwu ordered Xian to compile thirty-five scrolls of medical formulas, distributed throughout the realm to treat various illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu ordered him to compile thirty-five scrolls of prescriptions, distributed empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，以為太子詹事，委任甚厚。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was made Tutor to the Heir Apparent with heavy trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Tutor to the Heir Apparent with heavy trust.

sentences.zh: 上每幸東宮，顯常近侍，出入禁中，仍奉醫藥。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor visited the Eastern Palace, Xian was constantly in close attendance, entering and leaving the forbidden precincts, still attending to medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor visited the Eastern Palace, Xian attended closely, still practicing medicine within the palace.

sentences.zh: 賞賜累加，為立館宇，寵振當時。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts were repeatedly added; a residence was built for him; his favor shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards piled up and a residence was built for him; his favor was unmatched in his day.

sentences.zh: 以營療功，封衛國縣伯。

translations.literal: For merits in medical treatment he was enfeoffed as Baron of Weiguo County.
translations.idiomatic: For his medical achievements he was enfeoffed as Baron of Weiguo County.

sentences.zh: 及宣武崩，明帝踐阼，顯參奉璽策，隨從臨哭，微為憂懼。

translations.literal: When Xuanwu died and Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Xian participated in presenting the imperial seal and edict, followed to mourn at the funeral, and was slightly worried and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died and Emperor Ming took the throne, Xian took part in presenting the imperial seal and edict and attended the funeral rites—slightly uneasy and afraid.

sentences.zh: 顯既蒙任遇，兼為法官，恃勢使威，為時所疾。

translations.literal: Xian, having received favor and appointment, also served as a legal official; relying on power he wielded authority, and was resented by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Now favored and also serving as a judicial official, Xian relied on his power to throw his weight around, and people of the time resented him.

sentences.zh: 朝宰托以侍療無效，執之禁中。

translations.literal: A chief minister cited ineffectiveness in attending treatment as pretext and had him seized in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister seized on the claim that his medical attendance had failed, and had him detained in the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔削爵位，徙朔州。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his noble rank and exiled him to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped his title and sent him into exile at Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 臨執呼冤，直閣伊盆生以刀鐶撞其腋下，傷中吐血，至右衛府，一宿死。

translations.literal: As he was being taken he cried out his innocence; Direct Attendant Yi Pansheng struck him under the arm with a blade ring, wounding him to the core so that he vomited blood; he reached the Right Guard Office and died within one night.
translations.idiomatic: As he was seized he shouted that he was innocent; Direct Attendant Yi Pansheng struck him under the arm with a blade ring, wounding him grievously so that he vomited blood; he reached the Right Guard Office and died overnight.

sentences.zh: 子曄，尚書儀曹郎中，懼走，後被獲，拷掠百餘。

translations.literal: His son Ye, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Ceremonies, fled in fear; later he was captured and tortured over a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ye, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Ceremonies, fled in terror; he was later captured and flogged more than a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 宅沒於官。

translations.literal: His house was confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: His residence was confiscated by the government.

sentences.zh: 馬嗣明，河內野王人也。

translations.literal: Ma Siming was a man of Yewang in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Siming was from Yewang in Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少博綜經方，為人診脈，一年前知其生死。

translations.literal: From youth he broadly mastered medical classics and formulas; when taking people's pulses, he could know a year in advance whether they would live or die.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he mastered the medical classics; by reading a patient's pulse he could tell a year in advance whether they would live or die.

sentences.zh: 邢邵唯一子大寶，甚聰慧，年十七八患傷寒。

translations.literal: Xing Shao's only son Dabao was very intelligent; at seventeen or eighteen he fell ill with cold damage.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao's only son Dabao was very bright; at seventeen or eighteen he contracted typhoid fever.

sentences.zh: 嗣明為其診脈，退告楊愔云：「邢公子傷寒不療自差，然脈候不出一年便死。

translations.literal: Siming took his pulse; withdrawing, he told Yang Yin: "Young Master Xing's cold damage will resolve without treatment, yet the pulse signs indicate he will die within a year.
translations.idiomatic: Siming examined his pulse and afterward told Yang Yin, "The young Xing's cold damage will resolve on its own without treatment, but his pulse shows he will die within a year.

sentences.zh: 覺之少晚，不可復療。

translations.literal: Becoming aware of it a little late, it can no longer be treated.
translations.idiomatic: Because we realize it too late, nothing can be done to save him.

sentences.zh: 」數日後，楊、邢並侍宴內殿。

translations.literal: " A few days later, Yang and Xing both attended a banquet in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later, Yang and Xing both attended a banquet in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 文宣云：「邢子才兒大不惡，我欲乞其隨近一郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan said: "Xing Zicai's son Dabao is not bad; I wish to request for him a nearby commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan said, "Xing Zicai's son Dabao is quite promising. I want to ask that he be given a nearby commandery.

sentences.zh: 」楊以年少，未合剖符。

translations.literal: " Yang, citing his youth, said he was not yet fit to receive a seal of office.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang replied that the boy was too young to be entrusted with a commandery seal.

sentences.zh: 宴罷，奏云：「馬嗣明稱大寶脈惡，一年內恐死，若其出郡，醫藥難求。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, he memorialized saying: "Ma Siming says Dabao's pulse is bad and he may die within a year; if he goes out to a commandery, medicine will be hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet he reported: "Ma Siming says Dabao's pulse is poor and he may die within a year; if he is sent to a commandery, skilled medical care will be hard to find.

sentences.zh: 」遂寢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 大寶未期而卒。

translations.literal: Dabao died before the expected time.
translations.idiomatic: Dabao died before the year was out, just as Siming had predicted.

sentences.zh: 楊愔患背腫，嗣明以練石塗之，便差，因此大為楊愔所重。

translations.literal: Yang Yin suffered a swelling on his back; Siming coated it with refined stone paste and it was cured at once; for this he was greatly valued by Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin had a back swelling; Siming treated it with refined-stone paste and it healed at once, and Yang Yin came to hold him in great esteem.

sentences.zh: 作練石法：以粗黃色石如鵝鴨卵大，猛火燒令赤，內淳醋中，自有石屑落醋裏，頻燒至石盡，取石屑曝乾，搗下簁，和醋以塗腫上，無不愈。

translations.literal: The method for making refined stone: take coarse yellow stone about the size of a goose or duck egg, burn it fiercely until red, put it in pure vinegar—naturally stone fragments fall into the vinegar; burn repeatedly until the stone is exhausted; take the stone fragments, dry them in the sun, pound and sift them, mix with vinegar and apply to the swelling—none fail to heal.
translations.idiomatic: His refined-stone method: take coarse yellow stones about the size of a goose or duck egg, heat them in a fierce fire until red-hot, and drop them into pure vinegar, where stone fragments naturally fall off; repeat until the stones are used up. Dry the fragments in the sun, pound and sift them, mix with vinegar, and apply to the swelling—every case heals.

sentences.zh: 武平中，為通直散騎常侍，針灸孔穴，往往與《明堂》不同。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era he served as Regular Attendant Director of the Secretariat; in acupuncture points he often differed from the Mingtang classic.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuping era he served as Regular Attendant Director of the Secretariat; his choice of acupuncture points often differed from those in the Mingtang classic.

sentences.zh: 嘗有一家，二奴俱患，身體遍青，漸虛嬴不能食。

translations.literal: Once there was a household whose two servants both fell ill—their bodies turned blue all over, gradually becoming emaciated and unable to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Once a household had two servants who both fell ill; their bodies turned blue all over, they wasted away, and could not eat.

sentences.zh: 訪諸醫，無識者。

translations.literal: They consulted various physicians; none could diagnose it.
translations.idiomatic: They consulted physicians everywhere, but none could identify the illness.

sentences.zh: 嗣明為灸兩足趺上各三七壯，便愈。

translations.literal: Siming moxibusted each of the two insteps with twenty-one cones each, and they recovered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Siming applied twenty-one moxa cones to each instep, and both servants recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 武平末，從駕往晉陽，至遼陽山中，數處見榜，雲有人家女病，若能差之者，購錢十萬。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping, accompanying the imperial procession to Jinyang, in the mountains of Liaoyang he saw notices in several places saying a family's daughter was ill and offering one hundred thousand cash to whoever could cure her.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wuping era, while accompanying the emperor to Jinyang, he saw several notices in the Liaoyang mountains offering one hundred thousand cash to anyone who could cure a family's sick daughter.

sentences.zh: 又諸名醫多尋榜至是人家，問疾狀，俱不下手。

translations.literal: Moreover many famous physicians followed the notices to that household, inquired about the illness, and all refused to treat.
translations.idiomatic: Many famous physicians tracked down the notices and visited the family, but after examining the case none would treat her.

sentences.zh: 唯嗣明為之療。

translations.literal: Only Siming treated her.
translations.idiomatic: Only Siming undertook her treatment.

sentences.zh: 問其病由，雲曾以手持一麥穗，即見一赤物長二尺許，似蛇，入其手指中，因驚倒地，即覺手臂疼腫。

translations.literal: Asking the cause of her illness, she said she had once held a wheat ear in her hand and immediately saw a red thing about two feet long, like a snake, enter her finger; startled, she fell down, and at once felt pain and swelling in her arm.
translations.idiomatic: When he asked what had caused the illness, she said that once, holding a wheat stalk in her hand, she saw a red creature about two feet long, like a snake, enter her finger; she fell down in fright and immediately felt pain and swelling in her arm.

sentences.zh: 月餘日，漸及半身，肢節俱腫，痛不可忍，呻吟晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: After more than a month, it gradually spread to half her body; limbs and joints all swelled; the pain was unbearable and moaning continued day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the swelling spread to half her body; every limb and joint was swollen, the pain unbearable, and she moaned day and night without stopping.

sentences.zh: 嗣明即為處方，令馳馬往都市藥，示其節度，前後服十劑湯，一劑散。

translations.literal: Siming at once prescribed for her, ordered a horse gallop to the market for medicine, showed the dosage regimen; in all she took ten doses of decoction and one dose of powder.
translations.idiomatic: Siming immediately wrote a prescription, sent a rider to the market for medicine, and set out the dosage; she took ten doses of decoction and one dose of powder in all.

sentences.zh: 比嗣明明年從駕還，此女平復如故。

translations.literal: By the time Siming returned with the imperial procession the next year, this woman had fully recovered as before.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Siming returned with the imperial procession the following year, the woman had fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 嗣明藝術精妙，多如是。

translations.literal: Siming's medical skill was subtle and fine; many cases were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Siming's medical skill was extraordinary; many of his cases were like this.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于太子藥藏監。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as Superintendent of the Heir Apparent's Medicinal Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Kaihuang era of Sui while serving as Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Medicinal Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 然性自矜大，輕諸醫人，自徐之才、崔叔鸞以還，俱為其所輕。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was self-conceited and looked down on other physicians; from Xu Zhicai and Cui Shuluan onward, all were looked down on by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was arrogant by nature and looked down on other physicians; from Xu Zhicai and Cui Shuluan on, he held them all in contempt.

sentences.zh: 姚僧垣，字法衛，吳興武康人，吳太常信之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Yao Sengyuan, style name Fawei, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing, eighth-generation descendant of Yao Xinzhi, Grand Minister of Ceremonies of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Sengyuan, style name Fawei, was from Wukang in Wuxing Commandery, an eighth-generation descendant of Yao Xinzhi, Grand Minister of Ceremonies of Wu.

sentences.zh: 父菩提，梁高平令。

translations.literal: His father Puti was Magistrate of Gaoping under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Puti served as Magistrate of Gaoping under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 嘗嬰疾疹歷年，乃留心醫藥。

translations.literal: He once suffered from illness for years and thereupon turned his mind to medicine.
translations.idiomatic: After years of chronic illness he devoted himself to medicine.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝召與討論方術，言多會意，由是頗禮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang summoned him to discuss formulas and techniques; his words often matched the emperor's intent, and for this he was rather honored.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang summoned him to discuss medical methods; his answers often struck the emperor as apt, and Wu treated him with considerable respect.

sentences.zh: 僧垣幼通洽，居喪盡禮，年二十四，即傳家業。

translations.literal: Sengyuan from youth was thoroughly versed; in mourning he fulfilled every rite; at age twenty-four he inherited the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan was thoroughly learned from youth and observed mourning rites to the letter; at twenty-four he took over the family medical practice.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為太醫正，加文德主帥。

translations.literal: Serving Liang he was Chief Physician, with the additional title Master of Literary Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as Chief Physician with the additional title Master of Literary Virtue.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝嘗因發熱，服大黃。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang once, because of fever, took rhubarb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang once took rhubarb for a fever.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「大黃快藥，至尊年高，不宜輕用。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said: "Rhubarb is a strong medicine; Your Majesty is advanced in years and should not use it lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "Rhubarb is a powerful purge. Your Majesty is elderly and should not use it lightly.

sentences.zh: 」帝弗從，遂至危篤。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow his advice and eventually reached critical illness.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused to listen and soon fell critically ill.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，轉鎮西湘東王府中記室參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was transferred to Staff Officer in the Western Garrison, Prince of Xiangdong's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing he was transferred to Staff Officer in the household of the Prince of Xiangdong, Western Garrison Commander.

sentences.zh: 僧垣少好文史，為學者所稱。

translations.literal: Sengyuan from youth loved literature and history and was praised by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Sengyuan loved literature and history and was admired by scholars.

sentences.zh: 及梁簡文嗣位，僧垣兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang succeeded to the throne, Sengyuan also served as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang ascended the throne, Sengyuan also served as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝平侯景，召僧垣赴荊州，改受晉安王府諮議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang pacified Hou Jing, he summoned Sengyuan to Jingzhou and changed his appointment to Adviser in the Prince of Jin'an's household.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan of Liang suppressed Hou Jing, he summoned Sengyuan to Jingzhou and appointed him Adviser to the Prince of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝嘗有心腹病，諸醫皆請用平藥。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang once had an abdominal illness; all physicians recommended using mild medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang once suffered from abdominal illness; all the physicians recommended mild medicines.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「脈洪實，宜用大黃。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said: "The pulse is surging and full; rhubarb should be used.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "The pulse is surging and solid; rhubarb is indicated.

sentences.zh: 」元帝從之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 進湯訖，果下宿食，因而疾愈。

translations.literal: After the decoction was administered, old stagnant food was indeed expelled, and thereby the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the decoction, stagnant food was expelled as predicted and the illness was cured.

sentences.zh: 時初鑄錢，一當十，乃賜十萬貫，實百萬也。

translations.literal: At the time new coin was first cast, one coin counted as ten; he was granted one hundred thousand strings, which amounted to one million in old coin.
translations.idiomatic: New coin had just been introduced at ten times the old value; he was granted one hundred thousand strings—worth a million in old coin.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍克荊州，僧垣猶侍梁元，不離左右，為軍人所止，方泣涕而去。

translations.literal: When Wei armies captured Jingzhou, Sengyuan still attended Emperor Yuan, not leaving his side; stopped by soldiers, he wept and only then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei forces captured Jingzhou, Sengyuan still attended Emperor Yuan and would not leave his side; soldiers barred him and he departed only in tears.

sentences.zh: 尋而周文遣使馳驛徽僧垣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Emperor Wen of Zhou sent envoys by post-haste to summon Sengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Wen of Zhou sent messengers by urgent relay to summon him.

sentences.zh: 燕公於謹固留不遣，謂使人曰：「吾年衰暮，疾病嬰沉，今得此人，望與之偕老。

translations.literal: Duke of Yan Yu Jin firmly detained him and would not release him, telling the envoy: "I am aged and in decline, illness pressing heavily; now having obtained this man, I hope to grow old with him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yan Yu Jin refused to release him, telling the envoy, "I am old and gravely ill; now that I have this man, I hope to spend my remaining years with him.

sentences.zh: 」周文以謹勳德隆重，乃止。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen of Zhou, because Jin's merits and virtue were weighty, thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen, respecting Jin's great merit, did not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 明年，隨謹至長安。

translations.literal: The next year he followed Jin to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed Jin to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，授小畿伯下大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was appointed Junior Grand Master, Lesser Baron of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng he was appointed Junior Grand Master and Lesser Baron of Ji.

sentences.zh: 金州刺史伊婁穆以疾還京，請僧垣省疾，乃雲自腰至臍，似有三縛，兩腳緩縱，不復自持。

translations.literal: Jin Province Inspector Yi Lou Mu, returning to the capital due to illness, asked Sengyuan to examine him; he said from waist to navel it was as if there were three bindings, and his two feet were slack and could no longer support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Province Inspector Yi Lou Mu returned to the capital ill and asked Sengyuan to examine him; he said that from waist to navel it felt as though three bands were bound tight, and his legs had gone slack and would no longer support him.

sentences.zh: 僧垣即為處湯三劑，穆初服一劑，上縛即解；

translations.literal: Sengyuan at once prescribed three doses of decoction; when Mu first took one dose, the upper binding was immediately released;
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan immediately prescribed three doses of decoction; after the first dose the upper binding loosened;

sentences.zh: 次服一劑，中縛復解；

translations.literal: taking the next dose, the middle binding was again released;
translations.idiomatic: after the second dose the middle binding loosened;

sentences.zh: 又服一劑，三縛悉除。

translations.literal: taking another dose, all three bindings were completely removed.
translations.idiomatic: after the third dose all three bindings were gone.

sentences.zh: 而兩腳疼痹，猶自攣弱。

translations.literal: But the two feet were painful and numb, still cramped and weak.
translations.idiomatic: But his legs remained painful and numb, still cramped and weak.

sentences.zh: 更為合散一劑，稍得屈申。

translations.literal: He further compounded one dose of powder for him; gradually he could flex and extend.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan then prepared a powder formula; gradually Mu regained some ability to bend and straighten his legs.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「終待霜降，此患當愈。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said: "Wait until frost descends at last; this ailment should be cured.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "Wait until the frost comes; then this illness should be cured.

sentences.zh: 」及至九月，遂能起行。

translations.literal: " When the ninth month arrived, he was able to rise and walk.
translations.idiomatic: " By the ninth month he was able to rise and walk.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、襄樂公賀蘭隆先有氣疾，加以水腫，喘息奔急，坐臥不安。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief, Duke of Xiangle, Helan Long had had a qi illness beforehand, compounded by water swelling; panting was urgent, and whether sitting or lying he was not at ease.
