translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Helan Long, Duke of Xiangle, had long suffered from a respiratory illness complicated by edema; he breathed in ragged gasps and could find no rest sitting or lying down.

sentences.zh: 或有勸其服決命大散者，其家疑未能決，乃問僧垣。

translations.literal: Some urged him to take the Decisive-Life Great Powder; his family hesitated and could not decide, and so asked Sengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to take the powerful Decisive-Life Powder, but the family could not decide and consulted Sengyuan.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「意謂此患，不與大散相當。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said: "In my view this illness is not suited to the Great Powder.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "In my judgment this illness is not suited to the Great Powder.

sentences.zh: 」即為處方，勸急使服，便即氣通。

translations.literal: " He at once prescribed, urging immediate administration; at once his breath cleared.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote a prescription and urged immediate use; Long's breathing cleared at once.

sentences.zh: 更服一劑，諸患悉愈。

translations.literal: Taking another dose, all ailments were completely cured.
translations.idiomatic: After one more dose all his symptoms were cured.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、樂平公竇集暴感風疾，精神瞀亂，無所覺知。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief, Duke of Leping, Dou Ji suddenly contracted wind illness; his spirit was confused and chaotic, aware of nothing.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Dou Ji, Duke of Leping, was suddenly stricken with wind illness; his mind was clouded and he was wholly unaware of his surroundings.

sentences.zh: 醫先視者，皆云已不可救。

translations.literal: Physicians who examined him first all said he could no longer be saved.
translations.idiomatic: The physicians who saw him first all said he was beyond saving.

sentences.zh: 僧垣後至曰：「困矣，終當不死。

translations.literal: Sengyuan arrived later and said: "He is distressed, but in the end he will not die.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengyuan arrived he said, "He is gravely ill, but he will not die.

sentences.zh: 」為合湯散，所患即療。

translations.literal: " He compounded decoction and powder; the ailment was immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: " He prepared decoction and powder, and the illness was cured at once.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、永世公叱伏列椿苦痢積時，而不損廢朝謁。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief, Duke of Yongshi, Chifu Lie Chun suffered from severe dysentery for a long time, yet did not neglect attendance at court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Chifu Lie Chun, Duke of Yongshi, had suffered severe dysentery for a long time yet still attended court audiences without interruption.

sentences.zh: 燕公謹嘗問僧垣曰：「樂平、永世，俱有痼疾，意永世差輕。

translations.literal: Duke of Yan Jin once asked Sengyuan: "Leping and Yongshi both have chronic illnesses; I think Yongshi's is somewhat lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yan Yu Jin once asked Sengyuan, "Both Leping and Yongshi have chronic illnesses; I would think Yongshi's is the milder case.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「夫患有深淺，時有危殺，樂平雖困，終當保全；

translations.literal: " He replied: "Illnesses have depth and shallowness; at times there is mortal danger; Leping though distressed will in the end be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Illnesses differ in severity and in how dangerous they are at a given moment. Leping is gravely ill but will survive in the end;

sentences.zh: 永世雖輕，必不免死。

translations.literal: Yongshi though lighter, will inevitably not escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshi's case looks lighter, but he will certainly die.

sentences.zh: 」謹曰：「當在何時？

translations.literal: " Jin said: "When will it be?
translations.idiomatic: " Jin asked, "When?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不出四月。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Within the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Before the fourth month is out.

sentences.zh: 」果如其言，謹歎異之。

translations.literal: " It turned out as he said; Jin sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: " Events proved him right, and Jin marveled.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，遷遂伯中大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was promoted to Grand Master, Baron of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was promoted to Grand Master and Baron of Sui.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，文宣太后寢疾，醫巫雜說，各有同異。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, Empress Dowager Wenxuan fell ill; physicians and shamans offered mixed opinions, each differing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande Empress Dowager Wenxuan fell gravely ill; physicians and shamans offered conflicting diagnoses.

sentences.zh: 武帝引僧垣坐，問之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had Sengyuan sit and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu seated Sengyuan and asked his opinion.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣准之常人，竊以憂懼。

translations.literal: He replied: "By my reckoning compared with ordinary people, I privately feel worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "By my reckoning, compared with an ordinary case, I am deeply afraid for her.

sentences.zh: 」帝泣曰：「公既決之矣，知復何言！

translations.literal: " The emperor wept and said: "Since you have already decided it, what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept and said, "Since you have already made up your mind, what more is there to say!

sentences.zh: 」尋而太后崩。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 其後復因召見，乃授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Afterward he was again summoned and was then granted General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned again and granted the titles General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 敕停朝謁，若非別敕，不勞入見。

translations.literal: An edict stopped his attendance at court audiences; unless there was a separate edict, he need not enter for audiences.
translations.idiomatic: An edict excused him from court audiences; unless specially summoned, he need not appear.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝親戎東討，至河陰遇疾，口不能言；

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor personally led troops on an eastern campaign; reaching Heyin he fell ill and could not speak;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor personally led an eastern campaign; at Heyin he fell ill and could not speak;

sentences.zh: 瞼垂覆目，不得視；

translations.literal: eyelids drooped covering the eyes, and he could not see;
translations.idiomatic: his eyelids drooped over his eyes and he could not see;

sentences.zh: 一足短縮，又不得行。

translations.literal: one foot was shortened and contracted, and again he could not walk.
translations.idiomatic: one leg was shortened and cramped, and he could not walk.

sentences.zh: 僧垣以為諸藏俱病，不可並療，軍中之要，莫過於語，乃處方進藥，帝遂得言。

translations.literal: Sengyuan considered that all the viscera were afflicted and could not be treated together; in the army nothing mattered more than speech; he therefore prescribed and administered medicine, and the emperor was then able to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan judged that multiple organs were affected and could not all be treated at once; in camp nothing mattered more than the emperor's ability to speak; he prescribed medicine accordingly, and the emperor recovered his speech.

sentences.zh: 次又療目，目疾便愈。

translations.literal: Next he treated the eyes, and the eye illness was immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: Next he treated the eyes, and the eye ailment was cured at once.

sentences.zh: 未及足，足疾亦瘳。

translations.literal: Before he had yet reached the feet, the foot illness was also cured.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had even reached the leg, that ailment was cured as well.

sentences.zh: 比至華州，帝已痊復。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Huazhou, the emperor had fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Huazhou the emperor had fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 即除華州刺史，仍詔隨駕入京，不令在鎮。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Inspector of Huazhou, yet an edict ordered him to follow the imperial procession into the capital and not remain at his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed Inspector of Huazhou, but an edict ordered him to accompany the emperor to the capital rather than remain at his post.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，表請致仕，優詔許之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; a gracious edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he submitted a memorial asking to retire, and a gracious edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 是歲，帝幸雲陽，遂寢疾，乃召僧垣赴行在所。

translations.literal: That year the emperor visited Yunyang, then fell ill in bed, and summoned Sengyuan to the temporary imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor traveled to Yunyang, took to his bed with illness, and summoned Sengyuan to the imperial encampment.

sentences.zh: 內史柳昂私問曰：「至尊脈候何如？

translations.literal: Interior Secretary Liu Ang privately asked: "How is the Son of Heaven's pulse and condition?"
translations.idiomatic: Interior Secretary Liu Ang asked him privately, "How is the emperor's pulse?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「天子上應天心，或當非愚所及。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The Son of Heaven corresponds to Heaven's heart above; perhaps that lies beyond what a dull man can fathom."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Son of Heaven answers to Heaven above; that may lie beyond what a man like me can judge."

sentences.zh: 若凡庶如此，萬無一全。

translations.literal: If an ordinary commoner were in such a condition, not one in ten thousand would survive.
translations.idiomatic: Were an ordinary man in such a state, not one in ten thousand would recover.

sentences.zh: 」尋而帝崩。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 宣帝初在東宮，常苦心痛，乃令僧垣療之，其疾即愈。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was first in the Eastern Palace, he often suffered heart pain; he had Sengyuan treat it, and the illness was immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was still crown prince in the Eastern Palace, he often suffered from heart pain; Sengyuan treated him, and the ailment vanished at once.

sentences.zh: 及即位，恩禮彌隆。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, favor and courtesy toward him grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne, the honors shown him grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「嘗聞先帝呼公為姚公，有之？

translations.literal: He said to him: "I once heard the late emperor call you Duke Yao—is that so?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "I once heard my father call you Duke Yao—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣曲荷殊私，實如聖旨。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your subject has undeservedly received extraordinary kindness; it is indeed as Your Majesty says."
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan answered, "I have been favored far beyond my deserts; it is just as Your Majesty says."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此是尚齒之辭，非為貴爵之號。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "That was a term honoring your age, not a title of noble rank."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That was a term of respect for your years, not a noble title."

sentences.zh: 朕當為公建國開家，為子孫永業。

translations.literal: I shall establish a state and open a house for you—a perpetual inheritance for your descendants.
translations.idiomatic: I shall ennoble you with a fief and found a house that your descendants may hold forever.

sentences.zh: 」乃封長壽縣公。

translations.literal: " He was then enfeoffed as Duke of Changshou County.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon enfeoffed as Duke of Changshou County.

sentences.zh: 冊命之日，又賜以金帶及衣服等。

translations.literal: On the day of the investiture he was also granted a gold belt, garments, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his enfeoffment he was also given a gold belt, robes, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，除太醫下大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he was appointed Grand Physician, Lower Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang he was appointed Grand Physician with the rank of Lower Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 帝尋有疾，至於大漸，僧垣宿直侍疾。

translations.literal: The emperor soon fell ill, reaching the point of death; Sengyuan kept overnight duty attending the illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon fell gravely ill, and Sengyuan remained on night watch at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 帝謂隋公曰：「今日性命，唯委此人。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Duke of Sui: "Today's life and death I entrust to this man alone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Duke of Sui, "My life now rests in this man's hands alone."

sentences.zh: 」僧垣知帝必不全濟，乃對曰：「臣但恐庸短不逮，敢不盡心！

translations.literal: " Sengyuan knew the emperor could not fully recover; he therefore replied: "Your subject fears only that his mediocrity and inadequacy may fall short—but how could he fail to give his utmost!"
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan knew the emperor could not be saved. He answered, "I fear only that my poor skill may fall short—but how could I fail to give my all!"

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之。

translations.literal: " The emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 及靜帝嗣位，遷上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to Senior Opener of the Gate, General with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing succeeded to the throne, Sengyuan was promoted to Senior Opener of the Gate and General with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，進爵北絳郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang under Sui he was advanced to Duke of Beijiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era under Sui he was promoted to Duke of Beijiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 遺誡衣帢入棺，朝服勿斂，靈上唯置香奩，每日設清水而已。

translations.literal: He left instructions to be buried in his headcloth, not in court robes; on the bier only an incense casket was to be placed, with fresh water set out each day and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: He left orders to be laid in his coffin wearing only a headcloth, not court robes; on the bier nothing was to be placed but an incense box, with fresh water set out daily and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加荊、湖二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his original office and additionally made Inspector of Jing and Hu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former rank and additionally honored as Inspector of Jing and Hu provinces.

sentences.zh: 僧垣醫術高妙，為當時所推，前後效驗，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Sengyuan's medical skill was superb and esteemed by his contemporaries; cures before and after were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan's medical art was superb and universally admired; the cures he achieved, before and after, were beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 聲譽既盛，遠聞邊服，至於諸蕃外域，咸請托之。

translations.literal: Once his fame had grown great, it reached distant border regions; even various foreign domains all sought his help.
translations.idiomatic: As his renown spread, it reached the distant frontiers; even foreign lands beyond the borders sought him out.

sentences.zh: 僧垣乃參校徵效者為《集驗方》十二卷，又撰《行記》三卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Sengyuan then collated verified formulas into Collected Verified Prescriptions in twelve volumes, and also compiled Records of Practice in three volumes, both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan collated proven remedies into Collected Verified Prescriptions in twelve volumes and also wrote Records of Practice in three volumes; both works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 長子察，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His eldest son Cha has a biography in the Book of Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Cha has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 次子最，字士會。

translations.literal: His second son Zui, courtesy name Shihui.
translations.idiomatic: His second son was Zui, courtesy name Shihui.

sentences.zh: 博通經史，尤好著述。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories and especially loved writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply learned in the classics and histories and especially devoted to authorship.

sentences.zh: 年十九，隨僧垣入關。

translations.literal: At nineteen he followed Sengyuan into the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he followed Sengyuan west through the Pass.

sentences.zh: 明帝盛聚學徒，校書於麟趾殿，最亦預為學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming greatly gathered students and collated books at the Linzhi Hall; Zui also participated as an academy scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming gathered many students and set them to collating books in the Linzhi Hall; Zui also served among them as an academy scholar.

sentences.zh: 俄授齊王憲府水曹參軍，掌記室事，特為憲所禮接。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Water Bureau adjutant in Prince of Qi Xian's household, in charge of secretarial affairs, and was especially honored and treated well by Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Water Bureau adjutant in the household of Prince Xian of Qi, with charge of the secretariat, and Xian treated him with particular courtesy.

sentences.zh: 最幼在江左，迄于入關，未習醫術。

translations.literal: Zui had been young in the lands south of the Yangtze; until entering the Pass he had not studied medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Zui had grown up in the south and, until he entered the Pass, had never studied medicine.

sentences.zh: 天和中，齊王憲奏遣最習之。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era Prince of Qi Xian memorialized that Zui be sent to study it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era Prince Xian of Qi memorialized that Zui be sent to learn the art.

sentences.zh: 憲又謂最曰：「博學高才，何如王褒、庾信？

translations.literal: Xian also said to Zui: "In broad learning and high talent, how do you compare with Wang Bao and Yu Xin?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian also told Zui, "In breadth of learning and native talent, how do you compare with Wang Bao and Yu Xin?"

sentences.zh: 王庾名重兩國，吾視之蔑如，接待資給，非爾家比也。

translations.literal: Wang and Yu enjoy great fame in both states, yet I regard them as beneath notice; the welcome and support I show you surpass anything your family has known.
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Yu are famous in both realms, yet I think little of them; the welcome and support I give you are beyond anything your family has ever received.

sentences.zh: 勿不存心。

translations.literal: Do not fail to keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Do not neglect to bear this in mind.

sentences.zh: 且天子有敕，彌須勉勵。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven has issued an edict—you must strive all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the emperor himself has commanded it—you must apply yourself all the more.

sentences.zh: 」最於是始受家業，十許年中，略盡其妙。

translations.literal: " Zui thereupon began to inherit the family profession; within some ten years he had broadly mastered its subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: Zui then took up the family art, and within about ten years had largely mastered its depths.

sentences.zh: 每有人告請，效驗甚多。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone sought his help, cures were many.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone sought his aid, successful cures were numerous.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，除太子門大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui acceded, Zui was appointed Gate Grand Master to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Zui was appointed Gate Grand Master to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去官，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's death, grieving until he was wasted to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his father's death, grieving until he was wasted nearly to a skeleton.

sentences.zh: 既免喪，襲爵北絳郡公，復為太子門大夫。

translations.literal: Once mourning ended, he inherited the title Duke of Beijiang Commandery and again served as Gate Grand Master to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the title Duke of Beijiang Commandery and again became Gate Grand Master to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 俄轉蜀王秀友。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Companion to Prince of Shu Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to serve as Companion to Prince Xiu of Shu.

sentences.zh: 秀鎮益州，遷秀府司馬。

translations.literal: When Xiu was stationed at Yizhou, Zui was promoted to Secretariat Director in Xiu's princely household.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was posted to Yizhou, Zui was promoted to Secretariat Director in the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 及平陳，察至，最自以非嫡，讓封于察，隋文帝許之。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, Cha arrived; Zui, considering himself not the eldest legitimate son, yielded the enfeoffment to Cha, and Emperor Wen of Sui approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was conquered and Cha arrived, Zui, believing himself not the rightful heir, yielded the title to Cha, and Emperor Wen approved.

sentences.zh: 秀後陰有異謀，隋文帝令公卿窮其事。

translations.literal: Later Xiu secretly harbored treasonous designs; Emperor Wen of Sui ordered high officials to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiu secretly plotted rebellion, and Emperor Wen ordered the chief ministers to investigate the matter to its roots.

sentences.zh: 開府慶整、郝瑋等並推過於秀。

translations.literal: Opening-the-Gate Qing Zheng, Hao Wei, and others all shifted blame onto Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Zheng, Opener of the Gate, Hao Wei, and others all shifted the blame onto the prince.

sentences.zh: 最獨曰：「凡有不法，皆最所為，王實不知也。

translations.literal: Zui alone said: "Whatever was unlawful was all done by Zui; the prince truly knew nothing of it."
translations.idiomatic: Zui alone declared, "Every unlawful act was mine; the prince truly knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 」榜訊數百，卒無異辭，竟坐誅。

translations.literal: " After hundreds of lashings under interrogation, he never changed his story and was executed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: After hundreds of strokes under torture he never changed his account and was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 論者義之。

translations.literal: Commentators praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators honored him for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 撰《梁後略》十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Outline of the Later Liang in ten volumes, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Outline of the Later Liang in ten volumes, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 褚該，字孝通，河南陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Chu Gai, courtesy name Xiaotong, was a native of Yangdi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Gai, courtesy name Xiaotong, was from Yangdi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父義昌，梁鄱陽王中記室。

translations.literal: His father Yichang was Secretariat Director in the household of the Prince of Poyang under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yichang served as Secretariat Director in the household of the Prince of Poyang under Liang.

sentences.zh: 該幼而謹厚，尤善醫術。

translations.literal: Gai was careful and sincere from youth and especially skilled in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gai was careful and sincere, and especially skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，曆武陵王府參軍，隨府西上，後與蕭捴同歸周。

translations.literal: He served Liang, successively as adjutant in the Princely Household of Wuling; he followed the household westward, and later returned to Zhou together with Xiao Chou.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as adjutant in the household of the Prince of Wuling, followed the prince westward, and later returned to Zhou together with Xiao Chou.

sentences.zh: 自許奭死後，該稍為時人所重，賓客迎候，亞于姚僧垣。

translations.literal: After Xu Yi died, Gai gradually gained esteem among contemporaries; guests who came to visit ranked second only to Yao Sengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Yi died, Gai gradually won esteem among his contemporaries; visitors seeking him out ranked second only to Yao Sengyuan.

sentences.zh: 天和初，位縣伯下大夫，進授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he held the rank of Lower Grand Master of a County Marquisate; he was then promoted and granted General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianhe he held the rank of Lower Grand Master of a county marquisate, then was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 該性淹和，不自矜尚，但有請之者，皆為盡其藝術。

translations.literal: Gai's nature was gentle and mild; he did not vaunt himself, but whenever anyone sought him he fully exerted his art.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was gentle by nature and never boastful; whenever anyone sought him out he gave his full skill.

sentences.zh: 時論稱其長者。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised him as a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him as a man of upright character.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子則，亦傳其家業。

translations.literal: His son Ze also transmitted the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ze also carried on the family art.

sentences.zh: 許智藏，高陽人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zhicang was a native of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhicang was from Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 祖道幼，常以母疾，遂覽醫方，因而究極，時號名醫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daoyou, because his mother was often ill, therefore studied medical formulas and pursued them to their depths; he was styled a famous physician of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daoyou, moved by his mother's frequent illness, took up medical texts and pursued them to their depths; he was renowned as a master physician of his day.

sentences.zh: 誡諸子曰：「為人子者，嘗膳視藥，不知方術，豈謂孝乎。

translations.literal: He admonished his sons, saying: "As a son, one tastes food and inspects medicine; if one knows nothing of remedies, can that be called filial?"
translations.idiomatic: He warned his sons, "A son tastes his father's food and watches over his medicine; if he knows nothing of healing, can he be called filial?"

sentences.zh: 」由是，遂世相傳授。

translations.literal: " From this, the art was handed down through generations.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the art was passed down from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，位員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He served Liang, holding the post of Supernumerary Master of Cavaliers Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as Supernumerary Master of Cavaliers Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父景，武陵王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Consultation Adjutant in the household of the Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as Consultation Adjutant in the household of the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 智藏少以醫術自達，仕陳，為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Zhicang from youth made his way through medical skill; he served Chen as Master of Cavaliers Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicang rose early through his medical skill and served Chen as Master of Cavaliers Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 陳滅，隋文帝以為員外散騎侍郎，使詣揚州。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Emperor Wen of Sui appointed him Supernumerary Master of Cavaliers Attendant and sent him to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Emperor Wen appointed him Supernumerary Master of Cavaliers Attendant and sent him to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會秦王俊有疾，上馳召之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qin Jun fell ill, the emperor urgently summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Qin fell ill, the emperor urgently summoned him.

sentences.zh: 俊夜夢其亡妃崔氏泣曰：「本來相迎，如聞許智藏將至。

translations.literal: Jun dreamed at night that his deceased consort Lady Cui wept and said: "I had come to welcome you, but I hear Xu Zhicang is about to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Jun dreamed one night that his dead consort Lady Cui wept and said, "I had come to welcome you, but I hear Xu Zhicang is on his way."

sentences.zh: 其人若到，當必相苦，為之奈何？

translations.literal: If that man arrives, he will surely torment me—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: If he arrives, he will surely make things hard for me—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 」明夜，俊又夢崔氏曰：「妾得計矣，當入靈府中以避之。

translations.literal: " The next night Jun again dreamed Lady Cui said: "I have a plan—I shall enter the Bureau of Spirits to hide from him."
translations.idiomatic: The next night Jun dreamed again that Lady Cui said, "I have found a way—I shall enter the spirit realm to hide from him."

sentences.zh: 」及智藏至，為俊診脈曰：「疾已入心，即當發癇，不可救也。

translations.literal: " When Zhicang arrived, he felt Jun's pulse and said: "The illness has already entered the heart; seizures will soon follow—it cannot be saved."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhicang arrived he felt Jun's pulse and said, "The disease has reached the heart; convulsions will follow at once. There is no saving him."

sentences.zh: 」果如言，俊數日而薨。

translations.literal: " It proved as he said; Jun died within days.
translations.idiomatic: It happened just as he said; Jun died within a few days.

sentences.zh: 上奇其妙，齎物百段。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his skill and presented him with a hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at his skill and rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk and goods.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，智藏時致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Zhicang had already retired.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Emperor Yang took the throne, Zhicang had already retired.

sentences.zh: 帝每有苦，輒令中使就宅詢訪，或以輦迎入殿，扶登御床。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor suffered discomfort, he would send palace emissaries to inquire at his home, or have him brought by carriage into the hall and helped onto the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor fell ill, he sent palace envoys to inquire at Zhicang's home, or had him brought by carriage to the palace and helped onto the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 智藏為方奏之，用無不效。

translations.literal: Zhicang would prescribe formulas and submit them; none failed to take effect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicang would prescribe remedies and submit them; every prescription worked.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 宗人許澄，亦以醫術顯。

translations.literal: Clansman Xu Cheng also achieved renown through medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xu Cheng also won distinction through medicine.

sentences.zh: 澄父奭，仕梁，為中軍長史，隨柳仲禮入長安，與姚僧垣齊名，拜上儀同三司。

translations.literal: Cheng's father Yi served Liang as Chief Secretary of the Central Army; he entered Chang'an with Liu Zhongli and was as famous as Yao Sengyuan, and was appointed Senior Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's father Yi served Liang as Chief Secretary of the Central Army, entered Chang'an with Liu Zhongli, and was as famous as Yao Sengyuan; he was appointed Senior Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 澄有學識，傳父業，尤盡其妙。

translations.literal: Cheng had learning and knowledge; he inherited his father's profession and especially mastered its subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was learned and scholarly; he inherited his father's art and mastered its depths.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚藥典禦、諫議大夫，封賀川縣伯。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Director of Imperial Pharmacy and Remonstrance Grand Master, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hechuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of Imperial Pharmacy and Remonstrance Grand Master, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hechuan County.

sentences.zh: 父子俱以藝術名重于周隋二代，史失其事，故附云。

translations.literal: Father and son both were famed for their art through the Zhou and Sui dynasties; the histories lost their records, so they are appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were both famed for their art in the Zhou and Sui eras; because the histories omitted their deeds, they are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 萬寶常，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Wan Baochang—no one knows where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Baochang—of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 父大通，從梁將王琳歸齊，後謀還江南，事泄伏誅。

translations.literal: His father Datong followed the Liang general Wang Lin in surrendering to Qi; later he plotted to return to Jiangnan, the matter was exposed, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Datong followed the Liang general Wang Lin in surrendering to Qi; later he plotted to return to the south, the plot was discovered, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 由是寶常被配為樂戶，因妙達鐘律，遍工八音。

translations.literal: Because of this Baochang was assigned as a music-house household; through exquisite mastery of pitch and temperament he was adept in all eight tones.
translations.idiomatic: For this Baochang was assigned to a musicians' household; through his exquisite mastery of pitch and temperament he became skilled in all eight tones.

sentences.zh: 與人方食，論及聲調。

translations.literal: Once while eating with others, the conversation turned to musical modes.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while dining with others, the talk turned to musical pitch.

sentences.zh: 時無樂器，寶常因取前食器及雜物，以箸扣之，品其高下，宮商畢備，諧於絲竹，大為時人所賞。

translations.literal: There were no instruments at hand; Baochang therefore took the dishes before them and assorted objects, struck them with chopsticks, graded their pitches—the pentatonic notes were all complete, harmonizing like string and bamboo—and he was greatly admired by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: With no instruments at hand, Baochang took the dishes and assorted objects before them, struck them with chopsticks, and graded their pitches until the full pentatonic scale was present, harmonizing like strings and pipes; contemporaries marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 然曆周、隋，俱不得調。

translations.literal: Yet through Zhou and Sui alike he never received an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through both Zhou and Sui he never received an official post.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，沛國公鄭譯等定樂，初為黃鐘調。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Duke of Pei Zheng Yi and others fixed the music, initially setting it to the Yellow Bell mode.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang, the Duke of Pei Zheng Yi and others established the court music, initially in the Yellow Bell mode.

sentences.zh: 寶常雖為伶人，譯等每召與議，然言多不用。

translations.literal: Although Baochang was a musician-house performer, Yi and the others often summoned him to discuss matters, yet mostly did not adopt his views.
translations.idiomatic: Although Baochang was only a household musician, Zheng Yi and the others often summoned him to consult, yet seldom followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 後譯樂成，奏之。

translations.literal: Later when Yi's music was completed, it was performed for the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zheng Yi's music was finished, it was performed for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上召寶常，問其可不。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Baochang and asked whether it was acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Baochang and asked whether the music was acceptable.

sentences.zh: 寶常曰：「此亡國之音，豈陛下所宜聞！

translations.literal: Baochang said: "This is the music of a perishing state—how is it fitting for Your Majesty to hear it!"
translations.idiomatic: Baochang said, "This is the music of a doomed state—how can Your Majesty listen to it!"

sentences.zh: 」上不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 寶常因極言樂聲哀怨淫放，非雅正之音，請以水尺為律，以調樂器，其聲率下鄭譯調二律。

translations.literal: Baochang then spoke at length that the music was mournful, licentious, and dissolute—not the proper and upright sound; he requested to use a water-tube as a pitch standard to tune the instruments, and the pitch would generally fall two notes below Zheng Yi's tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang then argued at length that the music was mournful and dissolute, not the proper court sound; he asked to use a water-pipe as a pitch standard to tune the instruments, saying the pitch should fall two notes below Zheng Yi's tuning.

sentences.zh: 並撰《樂譜》六十四卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled the 《Music Treatise》 in sixty-four volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the 《Music Treatise》 in sixty-four volumes.

sentences.zh: 且論八音旋相為宮法，改弦移柱之變，為八十四調，一百四十律，變化終於一千八百聲。

translations.literal: It also discusses the method by which the eight tones rotate to serve as tonic notes, the changes of altering strings and shifting bridge-pillars, establishing eighty-four modes, one hundred forty pitch standards, with variations culminating in one thousand eight hundred notes.
translations.idiomatic: It also sets out the method by which the eight tones rotate as tonic notes, the technique of retuning strings and shifting bridge-pillars, eighty-four modes, one hundred forty pitch standards, and variations reaching one thousand eight hundred notes.

sentences.zh: 時以《周禮》有旋宮之義，自漢已來，知音不能通，見寶常特創其事，皆哂之。

translations.literal: At the time, because the 《Rites of Zhou》 contained the concept of rotating tonics, yet since Han no one versed in music could grasp it, when they saw Baochang independently creating this doctrine, all mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the 《Rites of Zhou》 spoke of rotating tonics, yet since Han no musician had been able to master the concept, when Baochang devised it on his own everyone mocked him.

sentences.zh: 至是，試令為之，應手成曲，無所疑滯，見者莫不嗟異。

translations.literal: On this occasion he was tested and told to perform it; at once he produced a composition with no hesitation, and all who witnessed it marveled.
translations.idiomatic: When he was asked to demonstrate, he produced a composition at once, without the slightest hesitation, and all who witnessed it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 於是損益樂器，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he modified musical instruments beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: He then redesigned musical instruments beyond number.

sentences.zh: 其聲雅淡，不為時人所好。

translations.literal: Its sound was refined and subdued, not favored by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The music was refined and subdued, and people of the day did not care for it.

sentences.zh: 太常善聲者，多排毀之。

translations.literal: Those skilled in music at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices mostly slandered and rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices mostly disparaged and rejected it.

sentences.zh: 又太子洗馬蘇夔以鐘律自命，尤忌寶常。

translations.literal: Moreover the Crown Prince's Groom Su Kui considered himself a master of pitch and temperament, and particularly resented Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kui, Groom of the Crown Prince, claimed expertise in pitch and temperament and particularly resented Baochang.

sentences.zh: 夔父威方用事，凡言樂者附之而短寶常。

translations.literal: Kui's father Wei was then in power; all who spoke on music attached themselves to him and belittled Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's father Su Wei was then in power, and everyone who spoke on music sided with him against Baochang.

sentences.zh: 數詣公卿怨望，蘇威因詰寶常所為，何所傳受。

translations.literal: Baochang repeatedly visited high officials to complain; Su Wei therefore interrogated him as to what he did and from whom he had received instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang repeatedly petitioned high officials with grievances, and Su Wei questioned him about his work and its source.

sentences.zh: 有一沙門謂寶常曰：「上雅好符瑞，有言征祥者，上皆悅之。

translations.literal: A Buddhist monk said to Baochang: "Your Majesty greatly favors omens and portents; anyone who speaks of auspicious signs pleases him."
translations.idiomatic: A monk told Baochang, "The emperor favors omens and portents; anyone who speaks of auspicious signs wins his favor."

sentences.zh: 先生當言徒胡僧受學，雲是佛家菩薩所傳音律，則上必悅。

translations.literal: "You, sir, should say you learned from a foreign monk, claiming that the pitch and temperament were transmitted by a Buddhist bodhisattva—then His Majesty will surely be pleased."
translations.idiomatic: "You should say you learned from a foreign monk, and that the pitch system was transmitted by a Buddhist bodhisattva—the emperor will surely be pleased."

sentences.zh: 先生當言，所為可以行矣。

translations.literal: "You, sir, should say that what you have done can be put into practice."
translations.idiomatic: "Tell him your work is ready to be adopted."

sentences.zh: 」寶常遂如其言以答威。

translations.literal: " Baochang then answered Wei just as the monk had advised.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang answered Su Wei as the monk had advised.

sentences.zh: 威怒曰：「胡僧所傳，乃四夷之樂，非中國宜行。

translations.literal: Wei angrily said: "What the foreign monk transmitted is the music of the four barbarian regions—not what China should adopt."
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei angrily said, "Music transmitted by a foreign monk is barbarian music—not fit for China."

sentences.zh: 」其事竟寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was ultimately shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 寶常聽太常所奏樂，泫然泣曰：「樂聲淫厲而哀，天下不久將盡。

translations.literal: Baochang listened to the music performed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and wept, saying: "The music is licentious, harsh, and mournful—the realm will soon perish."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Court of Imperial Sacrifices perform, Baochang wept and said, "This music is licentious, harsh, and mournful—the realm will not long endure."

sentences.zh: 」時四海全盛，聞言者皆謂不然。

translations.literal: " At the time the realm was at its height of prosperity; all who heard him disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was then at the height of its prosperity, and all who heard him dismissed the prediction.

sentences.zh: 大業之末，其言卒驗。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, his words were finally verified.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era, his prophecy came true.

sentences.zh: 寶常貧而無子，其妻因其臥疾，遂竊其資物而逃，寶常竟餓死。

translations.literal: Baochang was poor and childless; when he fell ill in bed, his wife stole his belongings and fled, and Baochang ultimately starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang was poor and childless; while he lay ill his wife stole his possessions and fled, and he starved to death.

sentences.zh: 將死，取其所著書焚之，曰：「何用此為？

translations.literal: About to die, he took the books he had written and burned them, saying: "What use is this?"
translations.idiomatic: As he was dying, he burned his manuscripts, saying, "What use are these?"

sentences.zh: 」見者於火中探得數卷，見行於世。

translations.literal: " Those present recovered several volumes from the fire, and they circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers rescued several volumes from the flames, and they circulated afterward.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，鄭譯、何妥、盧賁、蘇夔、蕭吉並討論墳籍，撰著樂書，皆為當時所用，至於天然識樂，不及寶常遠矣。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang, Zheng Yi, He Tuo, Lu Ben, Su Kui, and Xiao Ji all studied classical texts, wrote works on music, and were all used by the court of the day; yet in innate understanding of music, none approached Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang, Zheng Yi, He Tuo, Lu Ben, Su Kui, and Xiao Ji all consulted the classics and wrote treatises on music, and their work was adopted at court—but in innate musical insight none came close to Baochang.

sentences.zh: 安馬駒、曹妙達、王長通、郭令樂等能造曲，為一時之妙，又習鄭聲，而寶常所為，皆歸於雅。

translations.literal: An Maju, Cao Miaoda, Wang Changtong, Guo Lingyue, and others could compose music and were marvels of their age; they also practiced Zheng music, whereas what Baochang created all tended toward the refined.
translations.idiomatic: An Maju, Cao Miaoda, Wang Changtong, Guo Lingyue, and others were celebrated composers of their day and practiced the fashionable Zheng music, whereas Baochang's work always aimed at refinement.

sentences.zh: 此輩雖公議不附寶常，然皆心服，謂以為神。

translations.literal: Although in public discussion this group did not side with Baochang, they all inwardly acknowledged him and considered him divine.
translations.idiomatic: Though they did not publicly support Baochang, they all inwardly acknowledged his mastery and regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 時樂人王令言亦妙達音律。

translations.literal: At the time the musician Wang Lingyan also had exquisite mastery of pitch and temperament.
translations.idiomatic: The musician Wang Lingyan of the time also had exquisite mastery of pitch and temperament.

sentences.zh: 大業末，煬帝將幸江都，令言之子嘗于戶外彈胡琵琶，作翻調《安公子曲》，令言時臥室中，聞之驚起，曰：「變！

translations.literal: Near the end of Daye, when Emperor Yang was about to travel to Jiangdu, Lingyan's son once played a Central Asian pipa outside, performing a transposed version of the tune 《An Gongzi》; Lingyan was then in his bedchamber, and hearing it started up in alarm, saying: "Change!"
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye, as Emperor Yang prepared to travel to Jiangdu, Lingyan's son played a Central Asian pipa outside in a transposed version of 《An Gongzi》; Lingyan, resting in his bedchamber, started up in alarm and cried, "A change!"

sentences.zh: 變！

translations.literal: Change!
translations.idiomatic: A change!

sentences.zh: 」急呼其子曰：「此曲興自早晚？

translations.literal: " He hurriedly called to his son: "When did this tune arise?"
translations.idiomatic: He called urgently to his son, "When did this tune appear?"

sentences.zh: 」其子曰：「頃來有之。

translations.literal: " His son said: "It appeared only recently."
translations.idiomatic: His son answered, "Only recently."

sentences.zh: 」令言遂歔欷流涕，謂其子曰：「汝慎無從行，帝必不反。

translations.literal: " Lingyan then sighed and wept, telling his son: "Be careful not to follow the emperor on the journey—he will surely not return."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan sighed and wept and told his son, "Do not follow the emperor on this journey—he will never return."

sentences.zh: 」子問其故，令言曰：「此曲宮聲往而不反。

translations.literal: " His son asked the reason; Lingyan said: "In this tune the gong note goes forth and does not return."
translations.idiomatic: When his son asked why, Lingyan said, "In this tune the tonic note advances and does not return."

sentences.zh: 宮，君也，吾所以知之。

translations.literal: Gong is the ruler; that is how I know.
translations.idiomatic: The tonic stands for the ruler—that is how I know.

sentences.zh: 」帝竟被弑于江都。

translations.literal: " In the end the emperor was murdered at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor was murdered at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 蔣少游，樂安博昌人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Shaoyou was a native of Bochang in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shaoyou was from Bochang in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 魏慕容白曜之平東陽，見俘，入于平城，充平齊戶。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao of Wei pacified Dongyang, he was captured, sent to Pingcheng, and assigned as a household of the Pacification of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao of Wei pacified Dongyang, Jiang was taken captive, sent to Pingcheng, and registered as a household of the Pacification of Qi.

sentences.zh: 後配雲中為兵。

translations.literal: Later he was assigned to Yunzhong as a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: He was later assigned as a soldier in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 性機巧，頗能畫刻，有文思，吟詠之際，時有短篇。

translations.literal: By nature ingenious, he was quite skilled at painting and carving, had literary talent, and when composing verse occasionally wrote short pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Ingenious by nature, he was skilled at painting and carving, had literary sensibility, and sometimes composed short poems.

sentences.zh: 遂留寄平城，以傭寫書為業，而名猶在鎮。

translations.literal: He therefore remained in Pingcheng, earning a living by copying books for hire, while his name still remained on the garrison rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Pingcheng, earning his living as a copyist, while his name still lingered on the garrison register.

sentences.zh: 後被召為中書寫書生，與高聰俱依高允。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as a copying clerk in the Secretariat, and together with Gao Cong relied on Gao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned as a copyist in the Secretariat and, with Gao Cong, came under Gao Yun's patronage.

sentences.zh: 允並薦之，與聰俱補中書博士。

translations.literal: Yun recommended them both, and together with Cong he was appointed Secretariat Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun recommended them both, and he and Gao Cong were appointed Secretariat Erudites.

sentences.zh: 自在中書，恆庇于李沖兄弟子侄之門。

translations.literal: From the time he was in the Secretariat, he always found protection in the household of Li Chong and his brothers, sons, and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the Secretariat, he always found shelter under Li Chong and his brothers, sons, and nephews.

sentences.zh: 始北方不悉青州蔣族，或謂少游本非人士，又少遊微，因工藝自達，是以公私人望，不至相重，唯高允、李沖，曲為體練。

translations.literal: At first the north did not know the Jiang clan of Qingzhou; some said Shaoyou was not originally a gentleman, and because Shaoyou was lowly and had risen through craftsmanship, public and private regard did not accord him much respect—only Gao Yun and Li Chong treated him with full consideration.
translations.idiomatic: At first northerners did not know the Jiang clan of Qingzhou; some said Shaoyou was no true gentleman, and because he was of humble origin and had risen through craftsmanship, official and private opinion did not treat him with much respect—only Gao Yun and Li Chong showed him full consideration.

sentences.zh: 孝文、文明太后嘗因密宴謂百官曰：「本謂少游作師耳，高允老公乃言其人士。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming once at a private banquet told the officials: "We originally thought Shaoyou was merely a craftsman, but old Gao Yun says he is a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: At a private banquet Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming told the officials, "We thought Shaoyou was only a craftsman, but old Gao Yun insists he is a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」然猶驟被引命，以規矩刻繢為務，因此大蒙恩賜，而位亦不遷陟也。

translations.literal: " Yet he was repeatedly summoned to serve, with drafting, measuring, carving, and painting as his duties; because of this he received great favor and gifts, yet his rank was never promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was repeatedly summoned to serve, devoted to drafting, measuring, carving, and painting; he received generous rewards but his rank was never raised.

sentences.zh: 及詔尚書李沖與馮誕、遊明根、高閭等議定衣冠於禁中，少遊巧思，令主其事。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered Minister of the Interior Li Chong, together with Feng Yan, You Minggen, Gao Lu, and others, to determine ceremonial caps and robes within the inner palace, Shaoyou's ingenuity led them to put him in charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong, Feng Yan, You Minggen, Gao Lu, and others were ordered to determine ceremonial dress within the palace, Shaoyou's ingenuity put him in charge.

sentences.zh: 亦訪于劉昶。

translations.literal: They also consulted Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: They also consulted Liu Chang.

sentences.zh: 二意相乖，時致諍競，積六載乃成，始班賜百官。

translations.literal: Their two views conflicted, leading at times to heated disputes; after six years it was completed, and ceremonial dress was first distributed to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Their views conflicted and disputes arose; after six years the work was finished and the new dress first distributed to the officials.

sentences.zh: 冠服之成，不遊有效焉。

translations.literal: In the completion of caps and robes, Shaoyou—by the wordplay "not-you"—was effective.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou's contribution was essential to the completion of the ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 後於平城將營太廟太極殿，遣少遊乘傳詣洛，量准魏、晉基趾。

translations.literal: Later, when the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Hall of Supreme Ultimate were to be built at Pingcheng, Shaoyou was sent by fast courier to Luoyang to measure according to the foundations of Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Hall of Supreme Ultimate were to be built at Pingcheng, Shaoyou was dispatched by fast courier to Luoyang to take measurements from Wei and Jin foundations.

sentences.zh: 後為散騎侍郎，副李彪使江南。

translations.literal: Later he served as Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Writing Office and accompanied Li Biao as deputy envoy to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Writing Office and accompanied Li Biao on a mission to the south.

sentences.zh: 孝文修船乘，以其多有思力，除都水使者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen repaired ships and carriages, because he had great design ability he was appointed Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen undertook shipbuilding, Shaoyou was appointed Commissioner of Waterways for his design talent.

sentences.zh: 遷兼將作大匠，仍領水池湖泛戲舟楫之具。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Concurrent Master of Palace Construction, still overseeing the vessels and equipment for boating on the palace pools and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Concurrent Master of Palace Construction while continuing to oversee the pleasure boats and equipment on the palace pools and lakes.

sentences.zh: 及華林殿詔修舊增新，改作金墉門樓，皆所措意，號為妍美。

translations.literal: When Huayuan Hall was ordered restored and expanded and the Jinyong Gate tower rebuilt, all were designed by him and acclaimed as beautifully refined.
translations.idiomatic: When Huayuan Hall was restored and expanded and the Jinyong Gate tower rebuilt, he designed them all to acclaim for their elegance.

sentences.zh: 雖有文藻，而不得申其才用。

translations.literal: Although he had literary polish, he could not fully deploy his talents.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had literary gifts, he could not fully put his talents to use.

sentences.zh: 恆以剞劂繩尺，碎據匆匆，徙倚園、湖、城、殿之側，識者為之歎慨。

translations.literal: Constantly wielding carving tools and measuring cords, piecing together fragments in haste, he wandered beside gardens, lakes, city walls, and halls, and those who understood sighed for him.
translations.idiomatic: Constantly wielding carving tools and measuring cords, rushing from task to task, he wandered among gardens, lakes, walls, and halls, and those who understood his gifts sighed for him.

sentences.zh: 而乃坦爾為己任，不告疲恥。

translations.literal: Yet he calmly accepted it as his duty and never complained of fatigue or shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he accepted it calmly as his duty and never complained of fatigue or shame.

sentences.zh: 又兼太常少卿，都水如故。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with his post as Commissioner of Waterways unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining his post as Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、青州刺史，諡曰質。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous name Simple.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷餘。

translations.literal: He left a collected writings of more than ten chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings of more than ten chapters.

sentences.zh: 少遊又為太極立模範，與董爾、王遇等參建之，皆未成而卒。

translations.literal: Shaoyou also established models for the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; together with Dong Er, Wang Yu, and others he participated in its construction, but all died before it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou also created models for the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and worked on its construction with Dong Er, Wang Yu, and others, but all died before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 初，文成時，郭善明甚機巧，北京宮殿，多其制作。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Emperor Wencheng's reign, Guo Shanming was very ingenious; many of the northern capital's palaces were his work.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Emperor Wencheng's reign, Guo Shanming was very ingenious, and many palaces of the northern capital were his work.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，青州刺史侯文和亦以巧聞，為要舟，水中立射。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Governor of Qingzhou Hou Wenhe was also known for ingenuity; he built pleasure boats from which one could shoot targets standing in the water.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Qingzhou governor Hou Wenhe was also known for ingenuity; he built pleasure boats for archery at targets standing in the water.

sentences.zh: 滑稽多智，辭說無端，尤善淺俗委巷之語，至可玩笑。

translations.literal: Witty and clever, his speech was unpredictable; he was especially skilled in shallow, popular alley talk, amusing enough for jest.
translations.idiomatic: Witty and clever, his speech was unpredictable; he was especially skilled in popular street talk and banter.

sentences.zh: 位樂陵、濟南二郡太守。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Governor of Leling and Jinan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Leling and Jinan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 宣武、明帝時，豫州人柳儉、殿中將軍關文備、郭安興並機巧。

translations.literal: During the reigns of Emperor Xuanwu and Emperor Ming, Liu Jian of Yuzhou, Palace Guard General Guan Wenbei, and Guo Anxing were all ingenious.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Emperors Xuanwu and Ming, Liu Jian of Yuzhou, Palace Guard General Guan Wenbei, and Guo Anxing were all ingenious craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 洛中制永寧寺九層佛圖，安興為匠也。

translations.literal: When the nine-story pagoda of Yongning Temple was built in Luoyang, Anxing was the master craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine-story pagoda of Yongning Temple was built in Luoyang, Anxing was the master craftsman.

sentences.zh: 始孝文時，有范寧兒者善圍棋，曾與李彪使齊。

translations.literal: Beginning in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, there was Fan Ning'er, skilled at weiqi, who once accompanied Li Biao on a mission to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xiaowen's reign there was Fan Ning'er, skilled at weiqi, who once accompanied Li Biao on a mission to Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊令江南上品王抗與寧兒，制勝而還。

translations.literal: Qi had the Jiangnan master Wang Kang play against Ning'er; he won and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qi pitted the Jiangnan master Wang Kang against Ning'er; Ning'er won and returned home.

sentences.zh: 又有浮陽高光宗善樗蒲。

translations.literal: There was also Gao Guangzong of Fuyang, skilled at chupu.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Gao Guangzong of Fuyang, skilled at chupu.

sentences.zh: 趙國李幼序、洛陽丘何奴並工握槊。

translations.literal: Li Youxu of Zhao and Qiu Henü of Luoyang were both expert at woshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Youxu of Zhao and Qiu Henü of Luoyang were both expert at woshuo.

sentences.zh: 此蓋胡戲，近入中國。

translations.literal: This was originally a barbarian game that recently entered China.
translations.idiomatic: This was originally a foreign game that had recently entered China.

sentences.zh: 雲胡王有弟一人遇罪，將殺之，弟從獄中為此戲以上之，意言孤則易死也。

translations.literal: It is said a barbarian king had a younger brother who committed a crime and was to be executed; from prison the brother devised this game to present to him, meaning to say that one who stands alone is easily killed.
translations.idiomatic: A barbarian king's younger brother, condemned to death, is said to have devised this game in prison and sent it to the king, meaning that one who stands alone is easily killed.

sentences.zh: 宣武以後，大盛于時。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuanwu it flourished greatly in its time.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanwu it became extremely popular.

sentences.zh: 何稠，字桂林，國子祭酒妥之兄子也。

translations.literal: He Chou, courtesy name Guilin, was the nephew of the National University Chancellor Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou, courtesy name Guilin, was the nephew of National University Chancellor He Tuo.

sentences.zh: 父通，善琢玉。

translations.literal: His father Tong was skilled at carving jade.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong was skilled at jade carving.

sentences.zh: 稠年十餘，遇江陵平，隨妥入長安。

translations.literal: When Chou was just over ten, Jiangling was pacified; he followed Tuo to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou was just over ten, Jiangling fell; he followed He Tuo to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 仕周，禦飾下士。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as a lower officer in the Imperial Ornaments Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Zhou as a lower officer in the Imperial Ornaments Office.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，召補參軍，並掌細作署。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was prime minister, he was summoned as an adjutant and put in charge of the Fine Works Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was prime minister, Chou was summoned as an adjutant and put in charge of the Fine Works Office.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，累遷太府丞。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he rose to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 稠博覽古圖，多識舊物。

translations.literal: Chou broadly perused ancient diagrams and knew many antiquities.
translations.idiomatic: Chou studied ancient designs and was knowledgeable about antiquities.

sentences.zh: 波斯嘗獻金線錦袍，組織殊麗。

translations.literal: Persia once presented a brocade robe with gold thread, its weave exceptionally beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Persia once presented a gold-thread brocade robe of exceptional beauty.

sentences.zh: 上命稠為之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chou to make one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chou to replicate it.

sentences.zh: 稠錦成，逾所獻者，上甚悅。

translations.literal: When Chou's brocade was finished, it surpassed the tribute gift, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chou's brocade surpassed the tribute gift, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 時中國久絕琉璃作，匠人無敢措意，稠以綠瓷為之，與真不異。

translations.literal: At the time China had long ceased making glasswork, and craftsmen dared not attempt it; Chou made it from green porcelain, indistinguishable from the real thing.
translations.idiomatic: Glassmaking had long ceased in China and no craftsman dared attempt it; Chou made it from green porcelain, indistinguishable from the real.

sentences.zh: 尋加員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Writing Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Writing Office.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，桂州俚李光仕為亂，詔稠募討之。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, the Li tribesman Li Guangshi of Guizhou rebelled; an edict ordered Chou to raise troops and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaihuang, the Li chieftain Li Guangshi of Guizhou rebelled, and Chou was ordered to raise troops against him.

sentences.zh: 師次衡嶺，遣使招其渠帥，洞主莫崇解兵降款，桂州長史王文同鎖崇詣稠所。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Hengling, envoys were sent to summon the chieftains; the cave lord Mo Chong laid down arms and submitted, and Guizhou Administrator Wang Wentong bound Chong and brought him to Chou's camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Hengling, envoys summoned the chieftains; cave lord Mo Chong disarmed and submitted, and Guizhou Administrator Wang Wentong brought Chong in chains to Chou's camp.

sentences.zh: 稠詐宣言曰：「州縣不能綏養，非崇之罪。

translations.literal: Chou falsely announced: "The prefecture and county could not govern and nurture properly—this is not Chong's fault."
translations.idiomatic: Chou publicly declared, "The prefecture and county failed in governance—this is not Chong's fault."

sentences.zh: 」命釋之，引共坐，與從者四人，為設酒食遣之。

translations.literal: " He ordered Chong released, invited him to sit together, gave wine and food to him and his four followers, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He had Chong released, invited him to sit with him, served wine and food to him and his four companions, and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 大悅，歸洞不設備。

translations.literal: Greatly pleased, Chong returned to his cave without taking precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was greatly pleased; he returned to his cave without taking precautions.

sentences.zh: 稠至五更，掩及其洞，悉發俚兵以臨餘賊，象州逆帥杜條遼、羅州逆帥龐靖等相斷降款。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch Chou rushed his cave, mobilized all Li warriors against the remaining rebels, and rebellious chiefs Du Tiaoliao of Xiangzhou, Pang Jing of Luozhou, and others successively submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch Chou stormed the cave, mobilized Li warriors against the remaining rebels, and rebel chiefs Du Tiaoliao of Xiangzhou, Pang Jing of Luozhou, and others submitted in turn.

sentences.zh: 分遣建州開府梁昵討叛夷羅壽，羅州刺史馮暄討賊帥李大檀，並平之。

translations.literal: He separately dispatched Jianzhou Defender Liang Ni to suppress the rebellious Yi Luo Shou, and Luozhou Governor Feng Xuan to suppress rebel chief Li Datán—all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Jianzhou Defender Liang Ni against the rebel Yi Luo Shou and Luozhou Governor Feng Xuan against rebel chief Li Datán; both campaigns succeeded.

sentences.zh: 承制署首領為州縣官而還，眾皆悅服。

translations.literal: By imperial commission he appointed chieftains as prefectural and county officials and returned; all were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial commission he appointed chieftains as local officials and returned; all submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 有欽州刺史甯猛力帥眾迎軍。

translations.literal: Ning Mengli, Governor of Qinzhou, led his followers to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou governor Ning Mengli led his followers to welcome the army.

sentences.zh: 初，猛力欲圖為逆，至是惶懼，請身入朝。

translations.literal: At first Mengli had intended rebellion; now fearful, he asked to come to court in person.
translations.idiomatic: Mengli had once planned rebellion; now fearful, he asked to come to court in person.

sentences.zh: 稠以其疾篤，示無猜貳，放還州，與約八九月詣京師相見。

translations.literal: Chou, seeing his illness was grave, showed no suspicion and let him return to his province, arranging to meet at the capital in the eighth or ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Mengli was gravely ill, Chou showed no suspicion, let him return to his province, and arranged to meet at the capital in the eighth or ninth month.

sentences.zh: 稠還奏狀，上意不懌。

translations.literal: When Chou returned and reported, the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou reported back, the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，猛力卒，上謂稠曰：「汝前不將猛力來，今竟死矣。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month Mengli died; the emperor said to Chou: "You did not bring Mengli here before—now he has died after all."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Mengli died; the emperor told Chou, "You did not bring Mengli here when you could—now he is dead."

sentences.zh: 」稠曰：「猛力共臣約，假令身死，當遣子入侍。

translations.literal: " Chou said: "Mengli agreed with me that even if he died, he would send his son to serve at court."
translations.idiomatic: Chou said, "Mengli agreed with me that even if he died, he would send his son to serve at court."

sentences.zh: 越人性直，其子必來。

translations.literal: The Yue people by nature are straightforward; his son will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: The Yue are straightforward by nature—his son will surely come.

sentences.zh: 」初，猛力臨終，誡其子長真曰：「我與大使期，不可失信于國士，汝葬我訖，即宜上路。

translations.literal: " Earlier, at Mengli's deathbed, he admonished his son Changzhen: "I made an appointment with the envoy; one must not break faith with a man of the state. When you have finished burying me, you should set out at once on the road."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Mengli lay dying, he admonished his son Changzhen: "I gave my word to the envoy; one must not break faith with a man of honor. When my burial is complete, set out for the capital at once."

sentences.zh: 」長真如言入朝。

translations.literal: " Changzhen did as he said and entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhen did as instructed and came to court.

sentences.zh: 上大悅曰：「何稠著信蠻夷，乃至於此！

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "He Chou has kept faith even with the barbarians of the south—such that it has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased. "He Chou's trustworthiness even among the southern tribes has brought us to this!"

sentences.zh: 」以勳授開府。

translations.literal: " By his merit he was granted the office of Defender.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was granted the rank of Defender of the State.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，文獻皇后崩，稠與宇文愷參典山陵制度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, Empress Wenxian died; Chou and Yuwen Kai jointly managed the regulations for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Renshou era, after Empress Wenxian's death, Chou and Yuwen Kai jointly oversaw the design of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 稠性少言，善候上旨，由是漸見親昵。

translations.literal: Chou's nature was to speak little; he was good at discerning the emperor's intent, and thereby gradually came to be treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Chou spoke little but was skilled at reading the emperor's wishes, and gradually grew close to him.

sentences.zh: 上疾篤，謂稠曰：「汝既曾葬皇后，今我方死，亦宜好安置。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness was grave; he said to Chou: "You have already buried the empress; now that I am about to die, you should also make good arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay gravely ill, he told Chou, "You already arranged the empress's burial; now that I am dying, see that I am properly laid to rest as well."

sentences.zh: 囑此何益？

translations.literal: What use is there in entrusting this?
translations.idiomatic: What good will it do to tell you this?

sentences.zh: 但不能忘懷耳。

translations.literal: But I cannot forget—you understand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I cannot put it out of my mind, that is all.

sentences.zh: 魂而有知，當相見於地下。

translations.literal: If the soul has consciousness, we shall meet again in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have awareness, we shall meet again beneath the earth.

sentences.zh: 」上因攬太子頸曰：「何稠用心，我後事動靜當共平章。」

translations.literal: " The emperor then embraced the crown prince by the neck and said: "He Chou is devoted; you two shall jointly deliberate on all matters concerning my affairs after my death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then put his arm around the crown prince's neck. "He Chou is devoted to me; the two of you shall jointly decide all matters after my death."

sentences.zh: 大業初，煬帝將幸揚州，敕稠討閱圖籍，造輿服羽儀，送至江都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, Emperor Yang was about to visit Yangzhou; he ordered Chou to examine the archives and manufacture chariots, robes, and ceremonial regalia, and deliver them to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye era, when Emperor Yang prepared to visit Yangzhou, he ordered Chou to review the archives and produce chariots, vestments, and ceremonial insignia, to be sent to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 其日，拜太府少卿。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: That day he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Storehouses.

sentences.zh: 稠於是營黃麾三萬六千人仗，及車輿輦輅、皇后鹵簿、百官儀服，依期而就，送于江都。

translations.literal: Chou then organized thirty-six thousand yellow-banner guards, along with chariots, palanquins, the empress's full procession, and the ceremonial garments of all officials; everything was completed on schedule and sent to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chou then raised thirty-six thousand yellow-banner guards, plus chariots, palanquins, the empress's full retinue, and ceremonial robes for every official; all was finished on schedule and sent to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 所役工十萬餘人，用金銀錢物巨億計。

translations.literal: The workers conscripted numbered more than a hundred thousand; gold, silver, cash, and goods used amounted to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand workers were employed; gold, silver, currency, and supplies consumed ran to hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 帝使兵部侍郎胡雅、選部郎薛邁等勾覆，數年方竟，毫釐無舛。

translations.literal: The emperor had Vice Director of the Ministry of War Hu Ya, Selection Bureau Director Xue Mai, and others audit the accounts; it took several years to finish, with not the slightest discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Hu Ya of the Ministry of War and Xue Mai of the Selection Bureau audit the accounts; the review took years, yet not a single item was out of balance.

sentences.zh: 稠參會今古，多所改創。

translations.literal: Chou consulted past and present practice and made many innovations.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on past and present practice, Chou made many innovations.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以以來，皮弁有纓而無笄導。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, the leather cap had tassels but no hairpin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin times, the leather cap had tassels but no hairpin guide.

sentences.zh: 稠曰：「此古田獵服也，今服以入朝，宜變其制。

translations.literal: Chou said: "This is ancient dress for hunting in the fields; now that it is worn to enter court, its form should be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Chou said, "This is ancient hunting dress; if it is now worn at court, the design should be changed."

sentences.zh: 」故弁施象牙簪導，自稠始也。

translations.literal: " Hence an ivory hairpin guide was added to the cap—this began with Chou.
translations.idiomatic: An ivory hairpin guide was added to the cap—an innovation that began with Chou.

sentences.zh: 又從省之服，初無佩綬。

translations.literal: Again, the simplified ceremonial dress originally had no hanging sash worn at the belt.
translations.idiomatic: The simplified court dress, moreover, originally had no sash at the belt.

sentences.zh: 稠曰：「此乃晦朔小朝之服，安有人臣謁帝，而除去印綬，兼無佩玉之節乎？

translations.literal: Chou said: "This is dress for the brief assemblies at new and full moon—how can a minister attend the emperor having removed his seal sash and lacking the jade ornament as well?"
translations.idiomatic: Chou said, "This is dress for brief new- and full-moon audiences—how can a minister attend the emperor with neither seal sash nor jade ornament?"

sentences.zh: 」乃加獸頭小綬及佩一隻。

translations.literal: " Thereupon a small beast-head sash and a single ornament at the belt were added.
translations.idiomatic: A small beast-head sash and a single jade ornament were added.

sentences.zh: 舊制，五輅於轅上起箱，天子與參乘同在箱內。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the five ritual chariots had a box erected on the crossbar; the Son of Heaven and the attending ministers rode together inside the box.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, the five state chariots had a compartment built on the yoke; the emperor and attending ministers rode together inside it.

sentences.zh: 稠曰：「君臣同所，過為相逼。

translations.literal: Chou said: "Emperor and ministers in the same space—this presses too closely upon each other."
translations.idiomatic: Chou said, "Emperor and ministers sharing one space—that is too cramped and undignified."

sentences.zh: 」乃廣為盤輿，別構欄楯，侍臣立於其中。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made wide platform chariots, separately building railings; attending ministers stood within them.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore built wide platform chariots with separate railings, where attending ministers stood.

sentences.zh: 于內復起須彌平坐，天子獨居其上。

translations.literal: Within he further erected a Sumeru flat seat; the Son of Heaven sat alone upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, a raised Sumeru platform was added, where the emperor sat alone.

sentences.zh: 自餘麾幢文物，增損極多。

translations.literal: As for the remaining banners, flags, and ceremonial objects, additions and reductions were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Countless other banners, flags, and ceremonial objects were added or altered.

sentences.zh: 帝復令稠造戎車萬乘，鉤陳八百連。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Chou to build ten thousand war chariots and eight hundred linked Gouchen formations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Chou to build ten thousand war chariots and eight hundred linked Gouchen sections.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，以稠守太府卿，後兼領少府監。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; Chou was made Director of the Palace Storehouses, and later concurrently supervised the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved; Chou was made Director of the Palace Storehouses and later also Commissioner of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，攝左屯衛將軍，領御營弩手三萬人。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign, he served as acting General of the Left Garrison Guard, commanding thirty thousand crossbowmen of the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, he served as acting General of the Left Garrison Guard, leading thirty thousand imperial crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 時工部尚書宇文愷造遼水橋不成，師未得濟，左屯衛大將軍麥鐵杖因而遇害。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Works Yuwen Kai failed to build a bridge over the Liao River; the army could not cross, and Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard Mai Tiezhang was killed as a result.
translations.idiomatic: Work Minister Yuwen Kai had failed to bridge the Liao River; the army could not cross, and Grand General Mai Tiezhang of the Left Garrison Guard was killed in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 帝遣稠造橋，二日而就。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Chou to build the bridge; it was completed in two days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Chou to build the bridge, and it was finished in two days.

sentences.zh: 初，稠制行殿及六合城，至是，帝于遼左與賊相對，夜中施之。

translations.literal: Earlier Chou had designed a mobile palace and the Six Harmonies fortification; at this time, with the emperor facing the enemy east of the Liao, they were deployed at night.
translations.idiomatic: Chou had earlier designed a mobile palace and the Six Harmonies fortification; now, with the emperor facing the enemy east of the Liao, both were erected overnight.

sentences.zh: 其城，周回八里，城及女垣合高十仞，上布甲士，立仗建旗，四隅置闕，面列一觀，觀下三門，比明而畢。

translations.literal: The fort was eight li in circumference; wall and parapet together stood ten ren high; armed soldiers were deployed above, weapons raised and banners planted; towers were set at the four corners, a pavilion lined each face, and three gates opened beneath each pavilion—all completed by dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The fort measured eight li around; wall and parapet together stood ten ren high. Armored soldiers manned the top, weapons at the ready and banners flying. Towers rose at the four corners, a pavilion lined each face, and three gates opened beneath each pavilion—all finished by dawn.

sentences.zh: 高麗望見，謂若神功。

translations.literal: Goguryeo saw it and thought it divine workmanship.
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo forces saw it and took it for divine workmanship.

sentences.zh: 稍加至右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從幸江都，遇宇文化及亂，以為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Jiangdu, he encountered the rebellion of Yuwen Huaji and was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu, Yuwen Huaji's rebellion broke out, and he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及敗，陷於竇建德，復為工部尚書、舒國公。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji was defeated, he fell into the hands of Dou Jiande and again served as Minister of Works and Duke of Shu.
