translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji's defeat he fell into Dou Jiande's hands and again served as Minister of Works and Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 建德敗，歸於大唐，授少府監，卒。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande was defeated, he submitted to the Great Tang and was appointed Commissioner of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Jiande's defeat he submitted to the Tang and was appointed Commissioner of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories; he died thereafter.

sentences.zh: 又齊時有河間劉龍者，性強明，有巧思。

translations.literal: Also, in Qi times there was Liu Long of Hejian, strong and clear-minded by nature, with ingenious ideas.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi times there was also Liu Long of Hejian, a man of keen intellect and ingenious mind.

sentences.zh: 齊後主令修三雀台稱旨，因而曆職通顯。

translations.literal: Emperor Houzhu of Qi had him repair the Three Sparrows Tower to the emperor's satisfaction, and he successively rose through offices to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Houzhu of Qi had him restore the Three Sparrows Tower to the emperor's satisfaction, he rose steadily through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝踐阼，大見親委，位右衛將軍，兼將作大匠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui acceded to the throne, he was greatly trusted and appointed, serving as General of the Right Guard and concurrently Chief Architect.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he won great trust and was appointed General of the Right Guard and Chief Architect.

sentences.zh: 遷都之始，與高熲參掌制度，世號為能。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the capital relocation, he and Gao Jiong jointly managed institutional regulations, and the age hailed their ability.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the capital relocation, he and Gao Jiong jointly oversaw institutional design, and the age hailed their talent.

sentences.zh: 大業中，有南郡公黃亙及弟兗，俱巧思絕人，煬帝每令其兄弟亙少府將作。

translations.literal: In the Daye era there were the brothers Huang Gen, Duke of Nanjun, and Huang Yan, both of superhuman ingenuity; Emperor Yang frequently had the brothers successively hold the posts of Palace Storehouses and Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era there were Huang Gen, Duke of Nanjun, and his brother Yan, both possessed of extraordinary ingenuity; Emperor Yang often had the brothers alternate between the Palace Storehouses and the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 于時改創多務，亙、兗每參典其事。

translations.literal: At the time renovations were numerous; Gen and Yan each participated in managing these affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With renovations multiplying, Gen and Yan each assisted in these projects.

sentences.zh: 凡有所為，何稠先令亙、兗立樣，當時工人莫有所損益。

translations.literal: In whatever was undertaken, He Chou first had Gen and Yan prepare models; among the craftsmen of the day none could add or subtract anything.
translations.idiomatic: In every project, He Chou first had Gen and Yan prepare models; none of the craftsmen could improve upon them.

sentences.zh: 亙，位朝散大夫；

translations.literal: Gen held the rank of Grand Master of Palace Gentleman for Dispersed Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Gen held the rank of Grand Master for Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 兗，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Yan was Attendant Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Attendant Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陰陽卜祝之事，聖哲之教存焉，雖不可以專，亦不可得而廢也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: As for matters of yin and yang, divination, and sacrificial prayer, the teachings of the sages preserve them; though one cannot devote oneself exclusively to them, neither can they be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Annalist says: Matters of yin and yang, divination, and prayer—the sages' teachings acknowledge them. They must not be made one's sole pursuit, yet neither can they be abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 徇於是者不能無非，厚於利者必有其害。

translations.literal: Those who pursue these things cannot be without fault; those who thickly pursue profit must have their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who indulge in such pursuits cannot escape error; those who chase profit too eagerly always suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《樂》所失也淺，故先王重其德；

translations.literal: The losses from the 《Odes》, 《Documents》, 《Rites》, and 《Music》 are shallow; hence the former kings valued their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Where the 《Odes》, 《Documents》, 《Rites》, and 《Music》 are neglected, the harm is slight; therefore the ancient kings emphasized moral cultivation.

sentences.zh: 方術伎巧所失也深，故往哲輕其藝。

translations.literal: The losses from arts of technique and craft are deep; hence the sages of old slighted these skills.
translations.idiomatic: Where arts of technique and craft are neglected, the harm runs deep; therefore the sages of old held such skills in low esteem.

sentences.zh: 夫能通方術而不詭於俗；

translations.literal: One who can master arts of technique yet not be eccentric in the ways of the world;
translations.idiomatic: To master the arts of technique without falling into vulgar eccentricity—

sentences.zh: 習伎巧而必蹈於禮者，幾于大雅君子。

translations.literal: who practices craft yet invariably treads within ritual—such a one approaches the noble gentleman of the Great Odes.
translations.idiomatic: and to practice craft yet always remain within the bounds of ritual—such a one approaches the noble gentleman of the Odes.

sentences.zh: 故昔之通賢，所以戒乎妄作。

translations.literal: Hence the wise men of old, for this reason, warned against reckless action.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the sages of old warned against reckless innovation.

sentences.zh: 晁崇、張深、殷紹、王早、耿玄、劉靈助、李順興、檀特師、由吾道榮、顏惡頭、王春、信都芳、宋景業、許遵、吳遵世、趙輔和、皇甫玉、解法選、魏甯、綦母懷文、張子信、陸法和、蔣升、強練、庾季才、盧太翼、耿詢、來和、蕭吉、楊伯醜、臨孝恭、劉祐、張胄玄等，皆魏來術藝之士也。

translations.literal: Chao Chong, Zhang Shen, Yin Shao, Wang Zao, Geng Xuan, Liu Lingzhu, Li Shunxing, Tan Teshi, Youwu Daorong, Yan Etou, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimu Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, Lu Fafa, Jiang Sheng, Qiang Lian, Yu Jicai, Lu Taiyi, Geng Xun, Lai He, Xiao Ji, Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, Liu You, Zhang Zhouxuan, and others—all were masters of arts and techniques from Wei times onward.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Chong, Zhang Shen, Yin Shao, Wang Zao, Geng Xuan, Liu Lingzhu, Li Shunxing, Tan Teshi, Youwu Daorong, Yan Etou, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimu Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, Lu Fafa, Jiang Sheng, Qiang Lian, Yu Jicai, Lu Taiyi, Geng Xun, Lai He, Xiao Ji, Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, Liu You, Zhang Zhouxuan, and others—all were masters of arts and techniques from Wei times onward.

sentences.zh: 觀其占候卜筮，推步盈虛，通幽洞微，近知鬼神之情狀，其間有不涉用於龜筴，而究人事之吉凶，如順興、檀特之徒，法和、強練之輩，將別稟數術，詎可以智識知？

translations.literal: Considering their observation of omens, divination and augury, calendrical calculation of surplus and deficiency, penetrating the obscure and the subtle, nearly knowing the feelings and forms of ghosts and spirits—among them were some who did not rely on tortoise shells and yarrow stalks, yet investigated the fortune and misfortune of human affairs, such as Shunxing, Tan Te, and their kind, Fafa, Qiang Lian, and their company—did they possess a separate endowment of numerical arts? How could this be known through mere intellect?
translations.idiomatic: In their observation of omens, divination, calendrical reckoning, and piercing insight into hidden truths—nearly grasping the nature of spirits—some among them did not rely on tortoise and yarrow at all, yet still divined human fortune and misfortune: men like Shunxing and Tan Te, Fafa and Qiang Lian and their kind. Did they possess some separate gift of numerological art beyond what intellect alone could explain?

sentences.zh: 及江陵失守，前巧盡棄，還吳無路，入周不可，因歸事齊，厚蒙榮遇。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, their former skills were entirely abandoned; there was no road back to Wu, entry into Zhou was impossible, so they submitted to Qi and received generous honor and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, their former skills were cast aside; they could not return to Wu, could not enter Zhou, and so submitted to Qi, where they were generously honored.

sentences.zh: 雖竊之以叨濫，而守之以清虛，生靈所資，嗜欲咸遣，斯亦得道家之致矣。

translations.literal: Though they obtained office through presumptuous overreach, they maintained themselves in clarity and emptiness, relying on what sustains living beings and casting off all cravings—this too attained the ultimate aim of the Daoist school.
translations.idiomatic: Though they reached office through opportunism, they preserved clarity and detachment, living on what sustains life and casting off all desire—this too approximated the Daoist ideal.

sentences.zh: 信都芳所明解者，乃是經國之用乎？

translations.literal: What Xindu Fang understood and clarified—was it truly useful for governing the state?
translations.idiomatic: Was what Xindu Fang mastered truly of use in governing the state?

sentences.zh: 周澹、李脩、徐謇、謇兄孫之才、王顯、馬嗣明、姚僧垣、褚該、許智藏方藥特妙，各一時之美也。

translations.literal: Zhou Dan, Li Xiu, Xu She, She's elder brother's son Sun Zhicai, Wang Xian, Ma Siming, Yao Sengyuan, Chu Gai, and Xu Zhicang were all exceptionally skilled in prescriptions and medicines—each the finest of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dan, Li Xiu, Xu She, Sun Zhicai, nephew of Xu She, Wang Xian, Ma Siming, Yao Sengyuan, Chu Gai, and Xu Zhicang were all master physicians—each the finest of his age.

sentences.zh: 而僧垣診候精審，名冠一代，其所全濟，固亦多焉。

translations.literal: Yet Sengyuan in diagnosis and examination was precise and thorough, his fame topping a whole generation; those he fully saved were indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sengyuan's diagnosis was exceptionally precise, his fame unrivaled in his age, and the lives he saved were indeed many.

sentences.zh: 而弘茲義方，皆為令器，故能享眉壽，縻好爵。

translations.literal: And by spreading this moral instruction, all became fine vessels; hence they could enjoy long life and be tethered to fine rank.
translations.idiomatic: By upholding proper moral training, they all became men of promise; hence they enjoyed long life and high honors.

sentences.zh: 老聃云「天道無親，常與善人」，於是信矣！

translations.literal: Laozi said, "The Way of Heaven is without partiality—it constantly assists the good person"—how true this is!
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said, "The Way of Heaven is impartial—it constantly aids the good." How true that proves here!

sentences.zh: 許氏之運針石，百載可稱。

translations.literal: The Xu family's skill with needles and stones can be praised for a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu family's mastery of acupuncture could be praised for a century.

sentences.zh: 寶常聲律之奇，足以追蹤牙、曠，各一時之妙也。

translations.literal: Baochang's marvels in pitch and measure were enough to follow in the footsteps of Ya and Kuang—each the marvel of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang's mastery of pitch and measure rivaled the ancients Bo Ya and Shi Kuang—each the finest musician of his day.

sentences.zh: 蔣、何以剞劂見知，沒其學思，藝成為下，其近是乎？

translations.literal: Jiang and He gained recognition through engraving and printing, yet suppressed their scholarly thought; when craft becomes the lower pursuit—is this not close to the mark?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and He won renown through carving and printing, yet buried their scholarly learning; when craft ranks below learning—is that not nearer the truth?

sentences.zh: 周時，有樂茂雅以陰陽顯，史元華以相術稱，並所闕也。

translations.literal: In Zhou times, Yue Maoya was famed for yin and yang, and Shi Yuanhua was renowned for physiognomy—both are omitted here.
translations.idiomatic: During Northern Zhou, Yue Maoya was noted for yin-yang arts and Shi Yuanhua for physiognomy—both are omitted from this account.
